questions.q: A key agile project team member takes a leave of absence in the middle of an iteration and will not return to work for a while. What should the project manager do next regarding the feature on which the team member was working? *

o.t: Assign the feature to another team member, and have them try to complete the feature by the end of this iteration.
Review team capacity and reassign the functionality to additional iterations as required.
Determine if the team member can work from home to complete the functionality.
Review the work in progress with the product owner to determine the next step.

questions.e: In agile project management, collaboration and communication are critical. When a key team member is suddenly unavailable, the project manager should work with the product owner to reassess priorities and determine the best course of action.

questions.q: For an agile pilot project, the sponsor arranged an early product demonstration for the customer. During the meeting, the customer realizes that a new feature will significantly improve the product. After collecting the new requirements, what should the project manager do? *

o.t: Assess the impact of the new requirements and initiate the change request process.
Work with the product owner and the rest of the team on updating the project backlog.
Assess the impact and communicate the updated product roadmap to the stakeholders.
Follow the change management plan to update the risk register so It accounts for the added scope.

questions.e: In agile projects, new requirements are handled through the product backlog. The project manager should collaborate with the product manager and the team to prioritize and incorporate the new feature into the backlog, ensuring it aligns with project goals and priorities.

questions.q: A project manager for a large project's agile team is developing new workflows to meet changing business needs. As the second sprint is running, the product owner and agile team begin to receive more details that impact the scope change of running items. The agile team requests a change in the sprint goals and sprint backlog items. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Create a parallel sprint to deliver the additional items.
Guide the agile team to add the new scope to the product backlog.
Pause the sprint to allow time to include the new items.
Moderate the expectations for sprint quality.

questions.e: In agile, new scope or changes are added to the product backlog to be prioritized and addressed in future sprints. This approach maintains the current sprint's focus and prevents disruption while still acknowledging and planning for new requirements.

questions.q: A contractor has been making small changes to the engineering specifications without submitting change requests. The contractor and the technical team did not discuss the changes with the project manager, and the modifications do not affect the budget and quality of the deliverable. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Report the violation to the change control board (CCB) and seek comprehensive approval for these modifications.
Update the change management plan to define the level of control required for these types of modifications.
Ask the quality control team to evaluate the modifications, but take no action because the associated quality risks are insignificant.
Request the engineering team to update the specifications to reflect the modifications made by the contractor.

questions.e: Reporting the violation to the Change Control Board (CCB) ensures that all changes are formally reviewed and approved, maintaining project integrity and compliance with established change control procedures. This prevents unauthorized modifications and ensures transparency and accountability in the project.

questions.q: A project manager is managing a hybrid project. A stakeholder has directly contacted a team member and has requested a change. Due to the request, the team member was distracted from their work, which caused a loss in productivity. What should the team member do? *

o.t: Inform the stakeholder that the correct procedure for new requirements is to provide it directly to the project manager.
Inform the scrum master about the stakeholder's request for a change and the impact this has had on productivity.
Inform the stakeholder that the correct procedure for new requirements is to provide it directly to the change control board (CCB).
Inform the scrum master so that the change can be discussed directly with the stakeholder.

questions.e: In a hybrid project, especially with Agile components, the Scrum Master plays a key role in shielding the team from distractions and ensuring that communication flows properly. Direct stakeholder interruptions can harm team performance, and it's the Scrum Master’s responsibility to handle such external influences.

questions.q: A project manager is acting as a scrum master in a hybrid project and is dealing with a conflict between team members. What strategy should be used to handle this conflict? *

o.t: Sort conflicts into two groups: positive and negative.
Place conflicts into categories: structural and interpersonal.
Place conflicts on a shared conflict list and ensure it is visible.
Review conflicts during daily Scrum so they are handled in a timely manner.

questions.e: Categorizing conflicts into structural (related to processes, resources, or organizational structure) or interpersonal (related to personalities, communication styles, or values) helps the project manager understand the root cause and address each type appropriately. Structural conflicts might require process or organizational changes, while interpersonal conflicts may need mediation or team-building activities.

questions.q: A large multi-year project requires highly skilled staff for successful deployment. The management team and the project sponsor have analyzed the resource requirements and agreed to have permanent staff hired for the project to avoid potential budget overrun. However there is a risk of staff turnover during the course of the project, which may have an impact on the delivery. Which two actions should the project manager take to mitigate this risk? (Choose two). *

o.t: Introduce a recognition program to motivate and reward resource performance.
Enhance the competencies of the project team through training, mentoring and coaching.
Increase the trained staff to create back-up for resources.
Meet with management to discuss dividing the project into smaller projects.
Convince senior management to hire third-party staff.

questions.e: A. Introduce a recognition program to motivate and reward resource performance: This helps retain staff by keeping them motivated and engaged, thereby reducing the likelihood of turnover. B. Enhance the competencies of the project team through training, mentoring, and coaching: Developing team members' skills ensures they are more competent and capable of handling a variety of tasks, which reduces the impact if any team member leaves.

questions.q: A sponsor and project manager found out that a vendor in a different time zone has delayed the delivery of its products and needs a close supervision until the project gets back on track. The only option is to relocate three key members of the project team to spend 6 months abroad. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Communicate to the whole team the decision to relocate team members abroad and the implications of doing so in the next project status meeting
Communicate individually with the affected team members to negotiate the decision and confirm their willingness to relocate
Communicate the decision to the human resources (HR) department so they can direct the project team members to be sent abroad
Communicate to the affected team members' manager and schedule a meeting to discuss the details of this assignment

questions.e: The project manager should communicate individually with the affected team members to negotiate the decision and confirm their willingness to relocate, as this is the most respectful and ethical way to handle the situation. Relocating team members abroad for six months is a major change that will affect their personal and professional lives, and the project manager should consider their needs, preferences, and concerns before making any final decisions. The project manager should also explain the rationale and benefits of the relocation, and offer any support or incentives that may facilitate the transition. Communicating to the whole team, the HR department, or the team members' manager may not be appropriate or sufficient, as the project manager should first consult with the team members directly and obtain their consent. These other communication options may also create unnecessary confusion, resentment, or resistance among the team members or other stakeholders.

questions.q: A project manager at a company is considering a high-performing junior member of the organization to be the new project manager for a current project. What should the project manager do to prepare for a recommendation to senior management? *

o.t: Compile key highlights featuring the team member from the meeting minutes.
Ask the team member to write a short biography listing their qualifications.
Gather project artifacts that demonstrate the team member's high performance.
Calculate the health of the projects on which the team member has worked.

questions.e: Gathering project artifacts that demonstrate the team member's high performance provides concrete evidence of their capabilities and achievements. This serves as a solid basis for making a recommendation to senior management, as it highlights the team member's proven track record through actual project outcomes and contributions.

questions.q: During an iteration of a project, a planned activity becomes more complex. The work should be delivered in t he shortest time possible. What approach should be used in this situation? *

o.t: The team facilitator gets support from external team members.
The team members bring in a specialist to help them
The product owner moves it to the product backlog.
The cross-functional team member work together to complete the activity

questions.e: In Agile projects, cross-functional teams are designed to handle such situations by leveraging their diverse skills and capabilities. When an activity becomes more complex, collaboration among team members ensures efficient and effective completion in the shortest time possible.

questions.q: A project manager has been moved to a new division and is in charge of an existing project in an unfamiliar domain. When attempting to gain an understanding of the risks for this agile project, what is the primary tool the project manager should employ? *

o.t: Probability assessments.
Collaborative discussions.
Workshops for risk avoidance.
Interview with the project champion.

questions.e: In an agile environment, collaboration and open communication are essential for identifying and understanding risks. Agile projects often rely on the team’s collective input to address uncertainties and adapt to changes in real time. Collaborative discussions, involving team members, stakeholders, and other relevant parties, provide valuable insights and help the project manager better understand the risks from multiple perspectives.

questions.q: Due to a company merger and acquisition process, the main stakeholder of a critical project has been changed. This new stakeholder complains that they were unaware of a delay on the project of which the rest of the stakeholders were aware. All the communications about the project are shared via email at the start of every week. How should the project manager address this situation? *

o.t: Send evidence to the new stakeholder that the project's status was sent according to the schedule.
Suggest that the new stakeholder review the project status before the next board meeting.
Share the communications management plan with the new stakeholder.
Discuss project requirements with the new stakeholder, and update the communications management plan.

questions.e: By discussing project requirements with the new stakeholder and updating the communications management plan, the project manager ensures that the stakeholder's information needs and preferences are understood and incorporated. This proactive approach addresses the communication gap, aligns the new stakeholder with existing processes, and prevents future misunderstandings.

questions.q: A project team is working on a relative-weighting approach to assess product features. The product features will be prioritized to highlight the benefits and bring value to the customer. What should the project manager ask the team to do? *

o.t: Perform collaborative work that is coordinated by the project manager.
Rely on the expert judgment of the product owner.
Use a market-based strategy.
Engage the project sponsor.

questions.e: Using a relative-weighting approach to assess product features benefits from the collaborative efforts of the project team. This ensures diverse perspectives and thorough analysis, leading to more accurate prioritization of features. The project manager's coordination helps streamline the process and ensures all relevant inputs are considered.

questions.q: During the initiating phase of a project, a key stakeholder requests frequent changes to the project scope. What should the project manager do to improve the stakeholder's engagement? *

o.t: Discuss the work breakdown structure (WBS) with the key stakeholder and refine the requirements.
Update the project backlog and discuss it with the key stakeholder.
Update the project charter and discuss it with the keystakeholder.
Discuss the project scope statement with the key stakeholder and build prototypes.

questions.e: Discuss the project scope statement with the key stakeholder and build prototypes because the project manager needs to address the stakeholder's changing requests while clarifying the project’s scope. The project scope statement is a key document that outlines the project's boundaries, deliverables, and objectives. By discussing it with the key stakeholder, the project manager can ensure that both parties have a clear understanding of the scope and can manage expectations. Additionally, building prototypes allows the stakeholder to visualize and interact with the product early on, which can help clarify their expectations and reduce frequent scope changes.

questions.q: A project for company A was successfully delivered within scope schedule and budget by the end of the last iteration. However, during the project celebration ceremony, one of the business stakeholders says they perceive the project as a failure as it did not add any business value. What should the project manager have done to avoid this perception? *

o.t: Involved the business stakeholders in the sprint review.
Defined product backlog priorities with the sponsor and key stakeholders to deliver business benefits.
Implemented a closing survey for key stakeholders.
Confirmed that there is a communications management plan in place to make business stakeholders aware of the success.

questions.e: To avoid the perception that the project did not add value, the project manager should have engaged key stakeholders early on to define clear, prioritized business objectives. By collaborating with the sponsor and key stakeholders, the project manager ensures that the project focuses on delivering tangible business benefits that align with stakeholder expectations. The product backlog should reflect these priorities to deliver value throughout the project.

questions.q: A product company is transforming the way it develops and releases products in the market. Executives believe that this is a high-risk initiative, and this initiative must be successful. What should the project manager do in this scenario? *

o.t: Develop a business case with assumptions for the new model.
Develop a communications management plan to inform the employees about the new business model.
Adopt an iterative rollout approach that delivers the highest business value earlier.
Develop a detailed sprint plan with clear deliverables.

questions.e: Adopting an iterative rollout approach allows the project to deliver incremental value and adjust based on feedback and results. This reduces risk by focusing on delivering high-value components early, allowing for continuous improvement and ensuring that the initiative meets its business goals."

questions.q: At the closing phase of the project, the project manager sends the completion reports to the client as a formal written document, indicating that the contract has been completed. The client refuses to approve the document since the defect rate is 0.1%. The project manager insists that it is an acceptable rate as the standard defect rate of the industry is 0.15%. What should have been done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: The acceptance criteria should have been properly defined in the contract.
The client requirements should have been clearly defined in the contract.
The Manage Quality process should have been appropriately conducted.
The project manager should have reviewed the standard industry defect rate.

questions.e: To avoid disputes during the closing phase, it is crucial to have clear and agreed-upon acceptance criteria defined in the contract. This ensures that both the project team and the client have a mutual understanding of what constitutes acceptable deliverables, including defect rates. Properly defined acceptance criteria provide a concrete basis for project completion and client approval, preventing disagreements.

questions.q: Which three of the following scenarios are impediments to which a scrum master should pay attention? (Choose three) *

o.t: A team member talking about a user story that is not on the Scrum board.
A team member talking about a user story that is on the Scrum board.
A technology that blocks agile capabilities.
A lack of team empowerment and an inability to self-organize.
A review of the backlog at daily standup meetings.

questions.e: A. A team member talking about a user story that is not on the Scrum board: This is an impediment because it suggests that tasks are being discussed that are not part of the agreed-upon scope, leading to potential confusion and scope creep. C. A technology that blocks agile capabilities: Technological barriers that prevent the team from working effectively in an Agile manner are significant impediments that need to be addressed. D. A lack of team empowerment and an inability to self-organize: One of the core principles of Agile and Scrum is the empowerment and self-organization of teams. Without this, the team's progress and effectiveness are hindered. Option E: does not directly block the team's progress.

questions.q: A project manager is struggling to figure out the performance of the project teams in an agile environment. For the same scope of work, team A has calculated 100 story points and team B has calculated 125 story points. Which team is performing better? *

o.t: Team A as they have calculated fewer story points than team B.
Team B as they have calculated more story points than team A.
The team that completes the most stories selected from the sprint backlog.
The team with the least amount of defects in their deliverables.

questions.e: In an Agile environment, delivering high-quality work is crucial. A team that produces work with the fewest defects demonstrates a high level of craftsmanship, adherence to quality standards, and effective processes. Therefore, the team with the fewest defects in their deliverables is performing better.

questions.q: A project manager has recently been assigned to an agile project and discovers that a contractor for the project does not have any experience with agile. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the project sponsor to replace the contractor since they do not have agile experience.
Issue a formal notice to the contractor to obtain an agile certification.
Consult the project team to understand the extent of the training needs for the contractor.
Instruct the contractor to receive agile training since the project has already started.

questions.e: Consulting with the project team to understand the extent of the contractor's training needs allows the project manager to assess the specific areas where the contractor may require support. This approach ensures that the contractor can be effectively integrated into the agile process and provided with the necessary training or guidance to perform their role, rather than resorting to more drastic measures, such as replacement or issuing formal notices. This fosters a collaborative environment and addresses the issue constructively.

questions.q: An organization is producing a product using a hybrid approach with several phases. Some of the phases are planned to be executed in predictive and some in agile. During the agile phase, the project manager notices that the team members sometimes unknowingly work on the same task. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Communicate the task assignments to the team members in a clear manner.
Verify that the product owner has made the task assignments clear.
Confirm that the agile coach has made the task assignments clear.
Verify that the team members have made the task assignments clear.

questions.e: In a hybrid approach, clear communication of task assignments is crucial to prevent duplication of work. The project manager should ensure that all team members are aware of their specific tasks and responsibilities to avoid confusion and overlapping efforts. This proactive communication helps in maintaining coordination and efficiency within the team.

questions.q: A contractor delivering construction services to a company is using agile principles to manage the project tasks. Engineers are producing frequent design changes due to new legislation. There is a risk the contractor may lose money due to resources waiting on design changes or performing rework. What should the project manager do to minimize the cost? *

o.t: Put the project on hold until all definitions are ready in order to avoid rework.
Review the backlog with the product owner and prioritize the tasks that are least likely to be affected by a change in legislation.
Capture the engineers' feedback at the daily meeting and communicate it to the product owner.
Cancel the project release resources, then start again when all the definitions are ready.

questions.e: By reviewing the backlog and prioritizing tasks that are less likely to be affected by legislative changes, the project manager can minimize the risk of rework and resource downtime. This approach allows the project to continue progressing on more stable tasks while awaiting further design changes, thereby reducing costs and maintaining productivity.

questions.q: During a regular review, the project manager of an agile project realizes that a key stakeholder is missing critical information about some features being developed. In order to improve communications and reduce the risk of deploying the wrong features, what should the project manager do? *

o.t: Assess the stakeholder's needs and communication style and propose a tailored approach with regular status reports and progress meetings.
Invite the stakeholder to the regular "show and tell" sessions so the stakeholder is aware of project progress and feedback can be gathered.
Conduct stakeholder remapping, evaluate stakeholders by their level of influence and interest on the project, and communicate accordingly.
Include the stakeholder on regular project communications so that decisions can be followed up closely.

questions.e: By assessing the stakeholder's needs and communication style, the project manager can tailor the communication approach to ensure the stakeholder receives critical information in the most effective way. Regular status reports and progress meetings provide consistent updates and opportunities for feedback, thereby reducing the risk of deploying the wrong features and ensuring the stakeholder remains well-informed and engaged.

questions.q: One of the main inputs required for a deliverable is missing due to a miscommunication between the vendor and the project manager. Because of the missed deliverable, the critical path of the project is extended. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Start an audit of the vendor's processes and procedures.
Review lessons learned from previous projects with this vendor.
Make a detailed analysis on vendor issues during the project.
Execute a contingency plan to address the issue with the vendor.

questions.e: Executing a contingency plan is the most immediate and effective action to address the issue caused by the missing deliverable. It allows the project manager to mitigate the impact on the project's critical path and keep the project on track. Contingency plans are pre-defined strategies for dealing with unforeseen issues, and utilizing them helps resolve the problem promptly while maintaining project momentum.

questions.q: A verbal announcement is made that the new team member joining the Scrum team has limited mobility. The scrum master is aware that some team members are unsure how the dynamics of the team will change. What should the scrum master do? *

o.t: Create a stakeholder engagement plan.
Design a communications management plan.
Update the team charter accordingly.
Set up a meeting to discuss accommodations the team will have to make.

questions.e: Setting up a meeting to discuss accommodations addresses the immediate concerns of the team members and ensures that the new team member's needs are met. This proactive approach fosters an inclusive environment, promotes understanding, and helps smoothly integrate the new team member into the Scrum team, thereby maintaining team dynamics and productivity.

questions.q: An agile project manager would like to convert the requirements document into epics, capabilities, features and stories. In how many iterations should the project manager estimate the story duration? *

o.t: Four iterations.
One iteration.
Two iterations.
Three iterations.

questions.e: In Agile, stories are typically estimated to fit within a single iteration (sprint). This practice ensures that each story is small enough to be completed within the iteration's timebox, helping to maintain a steady and manageable workflow. Estimating story duration for one iteration aligns with Agile principles of delivering incremental value and maintaining flexibility.

questions.q: A project team has recently finished a sprint for developing two features for a fleet management system. Although the team delivered the required features, they encountered several issues and conflicts during the sprint. Team members were upset about this experience and are now showing a lack of motivation due to what has occurred. What can the project manager do to help increase the team's motivation and engagement with the project ? *

o.t: Review sprint progress with the project team members.
Set up one-on-one meetings with the project team members.
Review sprint planning procedures with the project team members.
Perform a sprint retrospective with the project team members.

questions.e: A sprint retrospective is the ideal forum to discuss what went well, what didn't, and how processes can be improved. It provides a structured opportunity for the team to reflect on their experiences, address issues, and collaboratively develop solutions to prevent similar problems in the future. This helps resolve conflicts, improve team dynamics, and increase motivation and engagement with the project.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a software development project. Recently, team members have complained that during the last few daily standup meetings, a key stakeholder frequently interrupts, requests explanations, and proposes unplanned changes. This issue is frustrating the project team and slowing down the work. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Instruct the team to work as planned and ignore the stakeholder's requests.
Escalate the situation to upper management.
Add more team members to make up for any project delays.
Address the issue with the stakeholder and explain the situation.

questions.e: Addressing the issue directly with the stakeholder is the best approach. It allows the project manager to explain the purpose of the daily standup meetings: to provide quick status updates and identify any impediments, rather than to discuss detailed changes or new requests. This conversation can help set clear expectations and boundaries, reducing interruptions and allowing the team to focus on their work more effectively.

questions.q: After the project charter's approval, the project manager needs to work on detailed project requirements, constraints and assumptions with stakeholders. However, not all of the stakeholders are immediately available for a meeting in the short term. What should the project manager do in order to gather the information needed from stakeholders? *

o.t: Email, call, or meet with each stakeholder separately to obtain their input.
Conduct a meeting to build the project management plan with the stakeholders who are available.
Escalate to the project sponsor that not all stakeholders are available for a meeting.
Meet with the project management team to build the project management plan before consulting stakeholders.

questions.e: Reaching out to each stakeholder separately ensures that the project manager gathers all necessary information, regardless of their availability. This approach allows for flexibility in communication and ensures that all stakeholders' inputs are considered in the detailed project requirements, constraints, and assumptions. It helps maintain inclusiveness and ensures that no critical information is missed due to scheduling conflicts.

questions.q: Two team members were recently released from a project because the customer reduced the budget. However, the agile team is still receiving the same, if not more, work requirements as before. How should the agile project leader resolve this situation? *

o.t: Update the restriction log with the new team capacity.
Explain the new project requirements to the team.
Update the project budget with the released team members.
Explain the new team velocity to the customer.

questions.e: By explaining the new team velocity to the customer, the agile project leader sets realistic expectations about what the team can accomplish given the reduced capacity. Velocity is a measure of the amount of work a team can complete in a given iteration, and with fewer team members, this velocity will naturally decrease. Communicating this change helps the customer understand the impact of budget cuts on project deliverables and may prompt a discussion about adjusting the scope or timeline accordingly.

questions.q: An agile project is in its sixth iteration out of 10. After the iteration review, the team receives feedback from the stakeholders that could result in a change in the product. What two actions should the project manager take? (Choose two) *

o.t: Ask the stakeholders about the priority of this change.
Ask the product owner to review the product backlog.
Ask the team members to analyze the impact of this change.
Ask the sponsor to approve the change request.
Ask the team members to include the change in the next iteration.

questions.e: A. Ask the stakeholders about the priority of this change: Understanding the priority of the change is crucial as it helps assess its importance relative to other ongoing work. This will guide decision-making on how to best incorporate the change into the project and ensure that the most critical items are addressed first. B. Ask the product owner to review the product backlog: The product owner is responsible for managing the backlog. By reviewing it, the product owner can determine where the new change fits in with existing priorities. This ensures the backlog is up-to-date and aligned with both stakeholder feedback and project goals.

questions.q: A project manager is working in an organization that uses SAFe for scaling agile practices across multiple teams. One team follows the Kanban framework for managing their work. During the Program Increment (PI) planning session, the Kanban team struggles to commit to specific stories and features due to the nature of their continuous workflow. What should the project manager do to address this situation? *

o.t: Explain to the Kanban team that they must align their work with the iteration cadence and commit to specific deliverables.
Encourage the Kanban team to focus on delivering work items in priority order while ensuring they align with the Program Increment objectives.
Instruct the Kanban team to switch to a Scrum framework during PI planning to enable better synchronization with other teams.
Allow the Kanban team to continue operating independently since Kanban teams do not need to participate in PI planning.

questions.e: In the SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework) approach, different teams may use different Agile methodologies. While teams that use Scrum commit to stories during PI planning, Kanban teams work with a continuous flow of work and do not follow fixed iterations. By encouraging the Kanban team to prioritize work items and align them with the Program Increment objectives, the project manager ensures that the Kanban team is still contributing to the overall PI goals without forcing them to commit to specific timeboxed iterations. This helps integrate their work with the broader team goals while respecting the nature of their workflow.

questions.q: After 1 year into the life cycle of an ongoing residential project, an announcement was received from the municipality regarding a new regulation that will greatly impact the project's schedule and budget. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Perform a qualitative risk analysis and update the risk register.
Submit a change request through the Integrated change control process.
Update the issue log and discuss It in the next steering committee meeting.
Estimate the associated costs and increase the project budget accordingly.

questions.e: The Regulation Is a Realized Issue, Not a Risk: A risk refers to an uncertain event or condition that could impact the project. In this case, the regulation is not uncertain—it has already been announced, and its impact on the project schedule and budget is real and certain. Risks belong in the risk register for tracking, but this scenario has moved beyond risk and into the category of an actual change that impacts project baselines. Addressing the Impact of the Regulation: Since the regulation affects the schedule and budget, it triggers the need for formal approval of changes to these baselines. Updating the risk register is not sufficient because it doesn’t resolve the immediate and real issue at hand.

questions.q: During the last sprint review, the stakeholder complained that the product was missing many features they had been expecting. The project team argued that every increment met the acceptance criteria and was approved by the stakeholder. The cost performance index (CPI) of the project is 1.15 and the schedule performance index (SPI) is 1.43. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the project team to perform the modifications since the project budget and schedule can support them.
Ask the stakeholder to submit a change request to increase the budget and time for the modifications requested.
Explain to the stakeholder that since the acceptance criteria for every increment were met the project can be closed.
Analyze the reason for the gap in understanding with both sides and negotiate a solution.

questions.e: Analyzing the reason for the gap in understanding ensures that the project manager identifies the root cause of the stakeholder's complaints and the project team's perspective. This approach facilitates a discussion to clarify expectations and acceptance criteria, leading to a negotiated solution that aligns the stakeholder's expectations with the project deliverables. It helps prevent similar issues in future sprints and maintains a collaborative relationship with the stakeholders.

questions.q: The following table shows the business value created and the development effort required to implement various features in a product. Which feature should the team prioritize first? *

o.t: A
B
C
D

questions.e: Prioritizing Feature A, which has a higher business value-to-effort ratio, ensures that the team delivers the most value with the least amount of effort, optimizing the project's overall efficiency and impact. The higher ratio of business value is A: 6/2 = 3.

questions.q: During project planning, the project manager identifies a high degree of uncertainty in the project scope, cost, and schedule. The project team decides to use four key techniques to address this uncertainty: rolling wave planning, progressive elaboration, expert judgment, and decomposition. Which of the following best describes how these techniques interact during project planning? *

o.t: Rolling wave planning allows for scope details to emerge over time, while decomposition breaks deliverables into manageable tasks. Expert judgment and progressive elaboration validate and refine these tasks.

Decomposition ensures that all deliverables are broken down upfront, while rolling wave planning and progressive elaboration support execution. Expert judgment is used to adjust deliverables as risks emerge.
Progressive elaboration creates detailed project plans immediately, while expert judgment determines deliverables, and decomposition verifies all required tasks. Rolling wave planning handles risks.

Expert judgment helps estimate costs and schedules, while rolling wave planning and progressive elaboration ensure deliverables are defined after execution begins. Decomposition refines work during project execution.

questions.e: Rolling wave planning allows the project team to plan in phases, starting with high-level planning for early phases and progressively elaborating the plan as more details become available over time. Decomposition breaks down deliverables into smaller, more manageable tasks, helping the team focus on specific elements of the work. Expert judgment involves using expertise to validate and refine the tasks or decisions, ensuring that they are accurate and realistic. Progressive elaboration means continuously improving and detailing the project plan as more information becomes available, especially when there’s uncertainty in scope, cost, or schedule.

questions.q: A key stakeholder for a construction project has been spending a lot of time at the site and interrupting the team's efforts. What should the project manager do in this situation? *

o.t: Work to understand the key stakeholder's concerns and provide feedback in regular project status reports.
Arrange an ad hoc meeting to address the key stakeholder's concerns with team members.
Reinforce with the key stakeholder that the project is performing on schedule.
Escalate the situation to the project sponsor because the key stakeholder's behavior is impacting progress.

questions.e: By understanding the key stakeholder's concerns, the project manager can address the root cause of the stakeholder's frequent visits and interruptions. Providing feedback through regular project status reports keeps the stakeholder informed and reassured, reducing the need for excessive time spent on-site. This approach fosters better communication and collaboration, minimizing disruptions to the team's efforts.

questions.q: An agile project is running activities to define the minimum viable product (MVP). During the session, the project manager identifies some mandatory regulations but there is no consensus to include these regulations in the MVP because it may extend the duration of the project What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Train the team on the new regulations as requested by management.
Get commitment from the team to include all of the required regulations.
Ask the project sponsor to add more time to the project.
Share with participants the need to focus only on product functionality.

questions.e: Including mandatory regulations in the MVP is crucial, as failing to do so could result in non-compliance, legal issues, and potential project failure. The project manager should ensure that the team understands the importance of these regulations and gains their commitment to including them, even if it means extending the project duration. This approach ensures that the product meets all necessary legal and regulatory requirements from the outset

questions.q: A team is working on a hybrid project. Due to different interpretations of the project requirements, the deliverables are not aligned to the expectations. What steps should the project manager have taken to prevent this? *

o.t: Update the project management plan in order to get back on track.
Ensure the team receives continuous feedback from customers and users.
Submit a change request to adjust the project scope.
Ensure the team understands all additional project requirements.

questions.e: In a hybrid project, continuous feedback from customers and users is essential to ensure that deliverables align with expectations. This feedback loop helps identify misunderstandings or misalignments early, allowing for timely adjustments and ensuring the project remains on track to meet stakeholder needs. By regularly engaging with customers and users, the project manager can prevent discrepancies between deliverables and requirements.

questions.q: At a meeting to receive approval for the project management plan, a project manager realizes that there is so much detail in the presentation that many of the stakeholders are not actively engaged in the process. The stakeholders are agreeing to the scope, goals, and timelines without giving them substantial thought. How should the project manager proceed? *

o.t: Stop the meeting and reschedule for another time with a more concise presentation.
Set up information review sessions before reconvening another approval session.
Get approval and promise to email more information to the stakeholders to clarify the technical details.
Obtain approval as fast as possible and close the meeting.

questions.e: Setting up information review sessions before reconvening another approval session ensures that stakeholders have the opportunity to fully understand and engage with the project details. This approach allows stakeholders to digest the information at their own pace and come prepared with informed questions and feedback for the next meeting. It fosters a more collaborative and thoughtful approval process, ensuring that all aspects of the project management plan are thoroughly considered and agreed upon.

questions.q: A team member shares with their functional manager some negative details about the performance of another team member that was discussed during the retrospective. The project manager finds out about this discussion. What two actions should the project manager take? (Choose two) *

o.t: Contact the team member's functional manager and invite them to the next retrospective.
Meet with the entire team to review the ground rules about safe environments.
Meet with the product owner to talk about the situation.
Contact the team member to explain what information can be shared outside the team.
Meet with the sponsor to review the situation.

questions.e: B. Meet with the entire team to review the ground rules about safe environments: This ensures that all team members are reminded of the importance of maintaining a safe and confidential environment during retrospectives. It reinforces the trust within the team, encouraging open and honest communication. D. Contact the team member to explain what information can be shared outside the team: This action directly addresses the specific incident by clarifying the boundaries and expectations regarding the confidentiality of retrospective discussions, helping prevent future breaches and ensuring that team dynamics remain intact.

questions.q: An organization uses a predictive approach but is open to using some agile practices. The project manager was asked to recommend an agile practice to provide business value throughout the project. What should the project manager recommend? *

o.t: Time-boxed iterations to allow the testing team to thoroughly test the product increments.
Incremental delivery and frequent backlog refinement based on user feedback.
Iterative development and collection of frequent feedback from project team members.
Frequent retrospectives to ensure that lessons learned and improvement actions are implemented.

questions.e: Incremental delivery ensures that the project delivers business value throughout its lifecycle by frequently providing usable product increments. Frequent backlog refinement based on user feedback allows the team to continuously adjust priorities and incorporate stakeholder input, ensuring that the most valuable features are developed and delivered. This approach aligns well with both agile and predictive methodologies by providing flexibility and value delivery.

questions.q: A project for a new product launch is in a very initial stage and the requirements are evolving. Due to stiff competition in the market, the customer would like to launch the product keeping the scope flexible. The project team intends to start the work based on the forecast of a similar project delivered last year. Which project approach suits the scenario? *

o.t: Execute it as a Scrum project.
Execute it as a predictive project.
Execute it using the same approach as the reference project.
Execute it as a project with stage gates.

questions.e: Scrum is well-suited for projects where requirements are evolving and flexibility is needed. It allows for iterative development, regular feedback, and the ability to adjust the scope based on stakeholder input and market conditions. This approach aligns with the customer's desire to keep the scope flexible while delivering the product incrementally.

questions.q: A project manager must manage a virtual application control software team that is culturally and geographically diverse. The project manager wants to promote open collaboration in a realtime manner. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Provide a software for instant messaging.
Document all information on the team wiki.
Promote the use of remote site syndication.
Facilitate regular conference calls.

questions.e: Providing software for instant messaging promotes real-time, open collaboration among team members, regardless of their geographical and cultural differences. Instant messaging tools facilitate quick communication, immediate feedback, and efficient problem-solving, which are crucial for managing a virtual team effectively.

questions.q: During the execution of a maintenance project, the contractor submits an offer for additional work. The project manager realizes that the activities billed are included in the initial scope of work. What should the project manager do next in this situation? *

o.t: Review the project scope and negotiate with the contractor.
Refuse the offer as it is included in the initial project scope.
Review the project costs and communicate this to the project sponsor.
Submit a change request to approve the offer.

questions.e: Reviewing the project scope helps the project manager verify whether the additional work proposed by the contractor is indeed included in the initial scope. If the activities are part of the original scope, the project manager can then negotiate with the contractor to clarify the misunderstanding and ensure that the work is performed without additional charges. This approach ensures alignment with the initial agreement and prevents unnecessary costs.

questions.q: Early in a project, a team member failed to effectively communicate the reason for their absence from three team meetings. How should the project manager handle this situation? *

o.t: Reaffirm the required project obligations directly with the team member.
Ask the team member to explain the reason for the absences.
Assess the impact of the team member's absence on the task involved.
Send a formal letter to the team member stating that their absences are noted.

questions.e: This option focuses on directly addressing the issue with the team member and setting clear expectations going forward. Reaffirming project obligations ensures the team member understands their responsibilities regarding meeting attendance and communication. It's a constructive approach that aims to correct the behavior and prevent future occurrences.

questions.q: A project manager arranged a team-building activity to build and maintain teamwork, trust, and commitment due to internal team conflicts. Two months after completing the training, another situation is causing new delays in the project. What should the project manager do to address this concern? *

o.t: Ask human resources (HR) to coordinate another activity.
Reassess the team situation and provide a proper solution.
Inform HR about the situation and ask for support.
Meet with the team to explain that conflicts must be addressed and solved.

questions.e: Reassessing the team situation allows the project manager to understand the current issues and their root causes. This assessment helps in identifying the most appropriate and effective solution to address the new delays and conflicts. It ensures that the project manager takes a targeted approach to resolving the issue rather than applying a generic solution, leading to a more effective and lasting resolution.

questions.q: A project manager is having difficulty acquiring final acceptance of some deliverables from a stakeholder for reasons that seem to be outside of the project acceptance criteria. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Persuade this stakeholder using emotional intelligence skills to obtain acceptance.
Obtain final acceptance from another stakeholder who is also familiar with the project.
Escalate this issue to the project sponsor and ask for support in obtaining final stakeholder acceptance.
Create a project acceptance waiver noting the stakeholder’s concerns so they can be addressed later.

questions.e: When a stakeholder's refusal to accept deliverables is based on reasons outside the agreed-upon acceptance criteria, escalating the issue to the project sponsor is appropriate. The project sponsor has the authority and influence to help resolve such disputes and ensure that the project's formal acceptance criteria are upheld. This approach ensures that the issue is addressed at the appropriate level and helps in maintaining the integrity of the project management process.

questions.q: The vendor for a new IT data center project failed to follow the required cabling standards as stated in the requirements specification. The infrastructure manager and vendor were involved in an argument about the issue. What should the project manager do to resolve and prevent additional arguments? *

o.t: Monitor the interactions between the vendor and infrastructure manager going forward.
Host a meeting with the vendor and infrastructure manager to help resolve their disagreement.
Escalate the issue to the sponsor so appropriate action can be taken.
Instruct the vendor to correct the problem without additional arguments.

questions.e: This approach allows the project manager to facilitate a discussion and mediate the disagreement between the vendor and the infrastructure manager. By doing so, the project manager ensures that both parties fully understand the requirements and standards that need to be followed. It also helps clarify any misunderstandings, identify the root cause of the issue, and work towards a resolution that aligns with project goals, preventing future conflicts.

questions.q: During a project planning meeting, the customer is not sure how to build a brand new product and is worried about extra costs and work. The customer is asking the project manager for guidance. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Wait to start the project execution phase until all requirements and acceptance criteria are clear.
Ask the customer to include all of the requirements in the project charter to officially start the project planning phase.
Schedule a brainstorming session and select the top ten most important requirements.
In the planning meeting, focus on releasing a minimum viable product (MVP) quickly and getting feedback from the end users.

questions.e: Focusing on releasing a MVP quickly allows the project to start with a basic version of the product that includes the most essential features. This approach helps in getting early feedback from end users, which can then be used to refine and improve the product. It minimizes initial costs and work by avoiding over-commitment to detailed requirements that may change based on user feedback. This iterative process aligns with agile principles and helps manage uncertainty and customer concerns about extra costs and work.

questions.q: An agile senior project team member suddenly resigns from the organization. Following this departure, the remaining team members are having difficulty accessing information and are unable to complete a deliverable. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Ensured the project repository is up to date.
Updated the job descriptions for all team roles.
Provided specialist training for all team members.
Made an effort to reemploy the senior project team member.

questions.e: By ensuring that the project repository is up to date, the project manager can mitigate the risk of losing critical information when a team member resigns. An up-to-date repository provides a centralized location for storing project documents, code, and other essential information, making it accessible to all team members. This approach helps maintain continuity and allows the remaining team members to access the information needed to complete their deliverables.

questions.q: A project to develop a large hydropower plant is in the implementation phase and is managed using a hybrid approach. What should the project manager do to ensure full compliance of quality requirements during the execution phase? *

o.t: Analyze the quality requirements.
Plan quality management.
Continually survey the quality of the deliverable.
Set up quality policies and procedures.

questions.e: To ensure full compliance with quality requirements during the execution phase, the project manager should continually survey the quality of the deliverables. This involves regular inspections, testing, and monitoring to verify that the deliverables meet the established quality standards and requirements. This proactive approach allows for the identification and correction of any quality issues as they arise, ensuring that the project maintains high-quality standards throughout its implementation.

questions.q: For the purposes of quality assurance, a quality audit was conducted on the processes being used in the project execution plan. One of the nonconformance issues raised by the auditor was that attendance lists for the project risk review meetings were not available. Why is an attendance list important? *

o.t: It is standard practice on projects to conduct risk review meetings which should have records on meeting attendance.
The attendance list is evidence that risk review meetings were held with the appropriate project team members.
It is a record that shows the number of attendees in the meeting.
It is a document that is registered within the lessons learned register.

questions.e: An attendance list is important because it provides evidence that risk review meetings were conducted with the appropriate project team members present. This documentation ensures that the right people, who are responsible for identifying, assessing, and managing risks, were involved in the discussions, thereby validating the effectiveness of the risk management process.

questions.q: A project team member does not submit the project status report on time. The team member is frustrated about being required to complete the report. The team member believes that the report does not reflect the reality of the project, has too many pages, and will not be read by stakeholders. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Review the requirements of the report with the team member to redefine its purpose.
Escalate to the team member's functional manager that the report was not submitted as requested.
Instruct the team member to provide the report and document this in the performance review.
Reassign the report to another team member to prepare and submit it as requested.

questions.e: The best course of action is for the project manager to engage with the team member to understand their concerns and work together to redefine the purpose of the report. This approach aligns with the PMI's emphasis on collaboration, communication, and stakeholder engagement as key aspects of effective project management. By reviewing the report's requirements, the project manager can ensure that it serves its intended purpose and is valuable to stakeholders, while also addressing the team member's concerns about its relevance and length.

questions.q: The client will not agree to closure, claiming that the project team has not performed the code inspections mandated in the development contract. The project team has performed the code inspections, however the records are not complete. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Seek expert legal advice on the interpretation of the clauses in the contract.
Hold a meeting with the project team project sponsor and the client to agree to the further work required to close the project and add to lessons learned.
Close the project and hand over the deliverables to the client.
Hold a lessons learned workshop with the project team and project sponsor to avoid contractual compliance issues arising in future projects.

questions.e: Holding a meeting with all relevant parties ensures that there is a clear understanding of the client's concerns and provides an opportunity to agree on the necessary steps to close the project. This collaborative approach helps to resolve any outstanding issues, ensure compliance with the contractual requirements, and document lessons learned to prevent similar issues in future projects.

questions.q: Early in the execution phase, a project manager discovers that recent changes in enterprise environmental factors (EEFs) will severely reduce the implementation cost and shorten the project schedule. How should the project manager address this situation? *

o.t: Meet with the project team to decide how the remaining budget will be spent.
Keep the extra budget as management reserve until project closeout.
Give the team extra time to finish tasks within the original timeline.
Follow the project escalation policy and communications management plan.

questions.e: Following the project escalation policy and communications management plan ensures that any significant changes in enterprise environmental factors (EEFs) are properly communicated and managed according to the established procedures. This approach allows the project manager to inform stakeholders, seek necessary approvals, and make any required adjustments to the project plan, budget, and schedule in a controlled and transparent manner. This ensures that the project remains aligned with organizational goals and stakeholder expectations.

questions.q: A project manager just started managing agile projects. The project manager realizes that due to the lack of a clear definition of project objectives and definition of done (DoD), their colleague's projects have had many difficulties. Sponsors keep asking for more features and the projects have yet to be completed. What should the project manager do to avoid these issues? *

o.t: Arrange meetings to ensure every necessary task to complete the project is included in the project management plan.
Convince the project sponsor to incorporate quality experts so the product can be tested and accepted as completed.
Convince the product owner to approach the team and look for options to find a solution to the problem.
Schedule meetings with key stakeholders to build the agile project charter and set clear expectations for the project.

questions.e: Scheduling meetings with key stakeholders to build the agile project charter helps establish a clear understanding of the project objectives and sets expectations from the outset. This includes defining the project goals, objectives, and the definition of done (DoD), which are crucial for managing scope and ensuring that the project delivers the desired outcomes. Clear expectations help prevent scope creep and ensure that all parties are aligned on what constitutes project completion.

questions.q: A project manager was just assigned to a project as the leader of an experienced agile team. How should the project manager influence the team to accomplish the project objectives? *

o.t: Express trust in the team's ability to fulfill the necessary deliverables.
Assert judgment over the team.
Use a plan-driven approach in order to demonstrate control over the project.
Increase the amount of subject matter experts (SMEs) to get better results.

questions.e: Expressing trust in the team's ability to fulfill the necessary deliverables is crucial for empowering and motivating an experienced agile team. Trust fosters a collaborative and positive environment, enabling team members to leverage their expertise and self-organize to achieve project objectives. This approach aligns with agile principles, which emphasize team autonomy and accountability.

questions.q: A project manager receives a voicemail from a business analyst on the project team. The business analyst indicates that an internal stakeholder is upset that they were not included before the project began. The stakeholder is asking for an addition to the requirements traceability matrix. What should the project manager do to improve the stakeholder relationship? *

o.t: Consult the project scope document to make sure the addition is in scope.
Update the stakeholder engagement plan to ensure the stakeholder is included in the project stakeholder list.
Initiate a project change request so the change control board (CCB) can decide if it is in scope.
Engage the stakeholder to solicit more information before responding to the request.

questions.e: Engaging the stakeholder to solicit more information allows the project manager to understand the stakeholder's concerns and the specifics of their request. This approach helps build a positive relationship by demonstrating that the project manager values the stakeholder's input and is committed to addressing their concerns. It also ensures that the project manager has all the necessary information to make an informed decision about the requested addition to the requirements traceability matrix.

questions.q: A company's CEO has just returned from a conference on the use of artificial intelligence (Al) and would like the project manager to implement this technology in the organization. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Start developing a business case.
Start a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats (SWOT).
Engage stakeholders and allocate resources
Gather requirements from stakeholders

questions.e: The project manager should start by conducting a SWOT analysis to identify the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats associated with implementing AI in the organization. This will help the project manager recognize potential risks and challenges, allowing them to develop a plan to address them.

questions.q: During the course of a project, the team develops negative group behaviors and becomes unmotivated and unproductive. What should the project manager do to improve the project team's performance? *

o.t: Define and analyze performance metrics.
Escalate poor performance to functional managers.
Update the stakeholder engagement plan.
Conduct a root cause analysis session.

questions.e: Conducting a root cause analysis session helps identify the underlying issues causing negative group behaviors, as well as the lack of motivation and productivity within the team. By understanding the root causes, the project manager can effectively address these issues and implement appropriate solutions to improve the team's performance. This approach focuses on resolving the fundamental problems rather than just addressing the symptoms.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a project within a program. The high-level requirements of the project are known, but the priorities of some of the requirements are uncertain as they are interdependent on some other pipeline projects within the program. How should the project manager prepare for the next steps of the project? *

o.t: Escalate to the management team to increase the timeline based on the complexity of the project.
Wait for the other project estimates before planning the schedule.
Prioritize and estimate the milestones for the high-level requirements based on historical data.
Ask the project management office (PMO) to estimate the tasks for all the projects and share the project management plan

questions.e: Prioritizing and estimating the milestones for the high-level requirements based on historical data allows the project manager to make informed decisions and move forward with planning. This approach leverages past experiences and data to estimate timelines and prioritize tasks, ensuring that the project progresses even when some requirements remain uncertain. It helps set realistic expectations and provides a structured plan for the next steps of the project.

questions.q: An equipment vendor will implement a new production line for a client company. The year-long project will include 2- to 4-month long iterations; however, the client's project manager has no agile experience. How should the project manager ensure that the client is effectively represented in the daily meetings? *

o.t: Recommend agile training programs that best suit the client project manager's schedule.
Realign the project to a predictive approach to ensure optimal collaboration between the teams.
Propose a session tor essential agile Knowledge transfer for the client team to align with the daily meeting goals.
Provide the client project manager with agile best practice documents and web resources.

questions.e: Proposing a session for essential agile knowledge transfer helps ensure that the client's project manager and team understand the goals and processes of daily meetings in an agile framework. This approach provides tailored, practical knowledge that can be directly applied to the project, fostering better collaboration and alignment. It ensures that the client is effectively represented and engaged in the agile process, enhancing overall project success.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a strategic communication project that involves subject matter experts (SMEs), interns, and new recruits. The project manager discovers that the project is not gaining much traction due to knowledge gaps from the interns. The budget for training is exhausted and the project needs to be delivered without delay. Which two actions should the project manager take? (Choose two) *

o.t: Identify the sources and specifics of the knowledge gap from the interns and new recruits.
Hire more SMEs and inform the human resources manager to lay off the nonperforming interns and new recruits.
Initiate a project change request for additional budget to train the interns and new recruits.
Ignore the issues with the project and try to deliver the project successfully without asking for training funds.
Put the interns and new recruits into groups and assign a SME as a mentor.

questions.e: A. Identify the sources and specifics of the knowledge gap from the interns and new recruits: Understanding the specific knowledge gaps allows the project manager to address the exact issues that are hindering progress. This step is crucial for targeted problem-solving and ensuring that the project can move forward efficiently. E. Put the interns and new recruits into groups and assign a SME as a mentor: Assigning mentors to the interns and new recruits leverages the expertise of the SMEs to provide on-the-job training and guidance. This approach helps bridge the knowledge gaps without requiring additional budget for formal training and ensures that the project stays on track.

questions.q: While developing a new product, a key stakeholder expresses concern about insufficient information on product feature requirements. The product team disagrees and mentions that detailed requirements have been provided. What should the project manager do to handle this situation? *

o.t: Organize a discussion with the product team to clarify the missing information.
Redirect the stakeholder to discuss this request with the functional manager.
Record the new requirements and ask the product team to develop them.
Conduct new risk and scope analyses, identifying the missing information.

questions.e: Organizing a discussion with the product team to clarify the missing information helps address the stakeholder's concerns directly and ensures that any misunderstandings or gaps in communication are resolved. This approach fosters collaboration and alignment between the team and the stakeholder, ensuring that everyone has a clear understanding of the requirements and expectations. It also helps prevent potential delays or issues in product development by addressing concerns early.

questions.q: A project manager has been assigned to lead a project to deploy a new system. The stakeholders disagree on the project objectives and approach. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Create a roles and responsibilities matrix based on the project charter and ask the sponsor to share it with all stakeholders to provide credible authority.

Conduct scoping workshops with the project team to create a work breakdown structure (WBS), assign tasks to various entities share this with all stakeholders, and ask the team to complete their tasks as scheduled.
Conduct a general meeting with all stakeholders and review and address a list of activities for each of them.
Breakdown the situation to identify the root causes for the disagreement and then work with each stakeholder and participating entity on their exact roles and responsibilities.

questions.e: Identifying the root causes of the disagreement allows the project manager to address the underlying issues directly. By working with each stakeholder to clarify their roles, responsibilities, and expectations, the project manager can foster better understanding and alignment. This approach ensures that all stakeholders have a clear and shared vision of the project objectives and approach, leading to more effective collaboration and project success.

questions.q: A project sponsor receives project information and updates in a timely manner, but the sponsor is concerned because key information is missing in the reports. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Review the communication needs of key stakeholders.
Confirm that the project information is understood and feedback is received.
Determine communication methods, frequency, and level of detail.
Provide all project information to the stakeholder.

questions.e: Reviewing the communication needs of key stakeholders helps the project manager understand what specific information the sponsor and other stakeholders require. By tailoring the reports to meet these needs, the project manager can ensure that all relevant information is included and that stakeholders are fully informed. This approach addresses the sponsor's concerns directly and improves the effectiveness of project communications.

questions.q: While managing a project, the project manager has just noticed that the last several monthly invoices have been challenged by the client when they were clearly defined. The actual invoice payments received have also been late and were outside of the contracted payment schedule. Recent invoices have only been partially paid. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Add nonpayment to the issue log and keep tracking payments.
Hold a meeting with the client to address the issue.
Review past projects for payment-related lessons learned.
Conduct a meeting with the project team to update the procurement management plan.

questions.e: Holding a meeting with the client to address the issue directly allows the project manager to understand the reasons behind the client's challenges and late payments. This approach fosters open communication, helps resolve misunderstandings or disputes, and provides an opportunity to agree on a way forward. Addressing the issue proactively can lead to a more cooperative relationship and timely resolution of payment issues.

questions.q: At the end of a project, the project manager is asked to submit project documentation for an internal audit in response to regulatory requirements. What should the project manager have done at the beginning of the project to ensure that project documentation would fulfill these requirements? *

o.t: Conducted a document review.
Confirmed documentation requirements with stakeholders.
Updated the project templates.
Implemented a new change control policy.

questions.e: At the beginning of the project, confirming documentation requirements with stakeholders ensures that all necessary documentation is identified, prepared, and maintained in accordance with regulatory and stakeholder needs. This proactive approach ensures that the project manager understands and plans for compliance from the start, making it easier to fulfill these requirements at the end of the project.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a project in a company that is transitioning to agile. Not all stakeholders believe in the project, and some stakeholders would like the entire project defined and planned out early in the project. However the project sponsor needs a quick win to ensure the continuation of the project. What approach should the project manager use? *

o.t: An agile approach as this would provide working functionality earlier.
A predictive approach as this would please the senior stakeholders.
A hybrid project as this will mitigate stakeholders' concerns.
A predictive approach as this will show benefits for all stakeholders.

questions.e: Using a hybrid project approach combines elements of both agile and predictive methodologies, allowing the project manager to address the concerns of stakeholders who prefer detailed early planning while also providing quick wins to satisfy the project sponsor. This approach balances the need for early deliverables and flexibility with the desire for a structured and planned project, making it a suitable compromise for a transitioning organization.

questions.q: A project manager is managing a project aimed at providing incremental deliveries to the market every three months. The team has been assigned, and the product backlog was created and prioritized by the product owner. After four iterations, the product owner escalates complaints to the CEO because the product does not meet the product owner's expectations. What should the project manager have done to prevent this situation from happening? *

o.t: Implemented sprint reviews with the product owner and retrospectives with the team to minimize gaps.
Performed risk management analysis during daily scrums.
Reviewed the organizational process assets (OPAs) and lessons learned from similar projects.
Performed backlog grooming to ensure that acceptance criteria were being met.

questions.e: Implementing sprint reviews with the product owner allows for regular feedback and alignment on the product's development, ensuring that the increments meet the product owner's expectations. Retrospectives with the team help identify and address any issues or gaps in the process, promoting continuous improvement. These practices ensure that the product development stays on track and aligns with the product owner's vision and requirements.

questions.q: A project manager is managing the project's scope and creating a work breakdown structure (WBS) with the team members. How should the project manager organize the WBS? *

o.t: Cost oriented.
Deliverable oriented.
Customer oriented.
Team oriented.

questions.e: The Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) should be organized in a deliverable-oriented manner. This means breaking down the project into manageable sections based on the deliverables or outcomes rather than by cost, customer, or team. A deliverable-oriented WBS helps ensure that all project deliverables are identified, structured, and linked to project objectives, facilitating clear tracking and management of work progress.

questions.q: During the daily meetings with the team the project manager notices that a new team member is not making the expected progress on an assigned task. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the new team member to follow the team ground rules.
Ask an experienced team member to identify a replacement.
Ask the new team member to reassess their own capabilities.
Ask an experienced team member to coach the new team member.

questions.e: Asking an experienced team member to coach the new team member helps the new member get up to speed more effectively. Coaching provides guidance, support, and knowledge transfer, which can help the new team member overcome challenges and improve their performance. This approach fosters teamwork and helps integrate the new member into the team, ensuring they can contribute effectively to the project's progress.

questions.q: An organization is transitioning to an agile environment. The project manager finds that most of the team members are not familiar with an agile environment. What should the project manager do to address this concern? *

o.t: Change the approach with the team.
Meet with an agile coach to handle this issue.
Analyze the level of the team's agile maturity.
Support the team members' growth and development.

questions.e: Analyzing the level of the team's agile maturity helps the project manager understand the team's current knowledge, experience, and comfort level with agile practices. This assessment allows the project manager to identify specific areas where the team needs support and training.

questions.q: During project execution, the project manager notices that the work performance reports have deteriorated drastically in less than two weeks. The project team in country A is complaining about delays resulting from holidays occurring in country B that have impacted their project team How should the project manager handle this situation? *

o.t: Implement crashing to compress the schedule and improve the schedule performance index (SRI).
Implement fast-tracking to compress the schedule and improve the SPI.
Perform conflict management using the project's resource management plan.
Review the risk management plan to evaluate the probability and impact of these delays.

questions.e: When unexpected delays occur, especially those due to known or predictable events like holidays, the first step should be to refer to the risk management plan.
