This plan includes strategies for dealing with risks and uncertainties, including how to assess and respond to delays. Reviewing the risk management plan allows the project manager to evaluate the situation properly and decide on the best course of action based on the predefined risk responses.

questions.q: During the last sprint review the product owner stated that the product does not deliver any value. The project manager believes that the product meets all the provided specifications. The team feels confused by the product owner's statement. What should the project manager do when using a hybrid approach? *

o.t: Escalate the matter to the executive board so they can decide on next steps.
Prioritize the project backlog and ask the development team to fix the issues.
Review the project's benefits management plan with the product owner.
Ask the product owner to terminate the project as it is no longer aligned to the expected benefits.

questions.e: In a hybrid approach, it is essential to ensure that the project delivers value as expected. If the product owner feels that the product does not deliver any value, it is crucial to review the benefits management plan. This plan outlines the expected benefits and how they will be measured. By reviewing this plan with the product owner, the project manager can clarify any misunderstandings, realign expectations, and ensure that both the product specifications and the expected benefits are in sync.

questions.q: A global company hired a project manager for a new implementation at all of its sites. After reviewing the business case and project charter, the project manager notes that the project team has different locations and regions to consider. What should the project manager do to address this situation? *

o.t: Inform the steering committee of the situation and request additional resources.
Coordinate virtual and face-to-face meetings at each site to improve communication.
Coordinate virtual meetings to assess the project team's communication needs.
Inform the project sponsor of this situation and request cultural orientation training.

questions.e: This approach helps to identify any potential communication barriers, time zone differences, and other factors that may impact communication. Based on this assessment, the project manager can then develop a communication strategy that ensures all team members are well-informed and can collaborate effectively.

questions.q: As part of a temporary assignment, a project manager is leading a business project. During a daily status meeting, it is discovered that the project manager's former department has not completed a task. This is delaying the current iteration. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Create an entry in the impediment board and assign it.
Invite the project team to a swarming session to define a solution.
Leverage the network of the former department and ask for help.
Escalate the issue to the product owner to define the next steps.

questions.e: Invite the project team to a swarming session to define a solution is the correct response because swarming is an Agile technique where the team collectively focuses on resolving a single issue. In this case, the delay caused by the former department can be addressed by bringing the team together to brainstorm and solve the problem collaboratively. It allows for a quick resolution by leveraging the team's skills and knowledge, promoting ownership and teamwork.

questions.q: An agile project is starting its seventh out of eight iterations. In a planning meeting, the team realizes that an unidentified risk became an issue and the contingency reserve has to be used. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the sponsor to approve inclusion of an additional iteration to the project.
Ask the team to include the contingency plan in the iteration backlog.
Help the team review the project approach to initiate the corrective actions.
Ask the sponsor for money to implement the contingency plan.

questions.e: Since an unidentified risk has become an issue and the contingency reserve is being used, the project manager needs to help the team assess the situation, identify corrective actions, and ensure the project can continue to move forward with minimal disruption. The focus should be on solving the problem, not necessarily adding iterations or seeking more money right away. The goal is to manage the issue efficiently by reviewing the project approach and taking appropriate corrective actions.

questions.q: A project team has recently completed the initial sprint for developing an automated payroll system for a company. The project manager has scheduled a sprint planning meeting with the product owner and team members to discuss which features should be worked on next Which two pieces of information does the project manager need in order to make this meeting productive and effective? (Choose two) *

o.t: Sprint charter.
Burndown chart.
Company mission and vision.
Product backlog.
Sprint goal.

questions.e: Product Backlog: The product backlog is a prioritized list of features, enhancements, and bug fixes that are required for the product. It is essential for the sprint planning meeting as it provides the team with an overview of what needs to be worked on next. Sprint Goal: The sprint goal defines the objective for the upcoming sprint. It provides a clear focus and direction for the team, ensuring that everyone is aligned on what needs to be achieved by the end of the sprint. Having these two pieces of information allows the team to select the most important items from the product backlog that will help achieve the sprint goal, making the planning meeting productive and effective.

questions.q: A project manager has been assigned to complete a worksite project that was started by a different project manager. The project is now in the execution stage. Upon careful review, the project manager realizes that the local community was not included in the stakeholder register, which has resulted in extreme opposition from the community. How should the project manager handle this issue? *

o.t: Disregard these stakeholders since the relevant documents have been secured to execute this project.
Update the stakeholder register and risk management plan.
Update the stakeholder register and revise the stakeholder engagement plan.
Explain to the community members why they were not included as stakeholders for the project.

questions.e: In project management, it is crucial to identify and engage all relevant stakeholders to ensure project success. If the local community was not initially included in the stakeholder register and this has led to opposition, the project manager should: Update the Stakeholder Register: This ensures that the local community is formally recognized as a stakeholder. Revise the Stakeholder Engagement Plan: This involves creating or modifying strategies to effectively communicate with and involve the newly identified stakeholders to address their concerns and manage their expectations. By taking these steps, the project manager can mitigate the opposition from the local community and facilitate smoother project execution.

questions.q: A project manager is working with a Scrum team that is continually missing deadlines. The steering committee is concerned about the project as it is not clear that it will deliver the expected value. After some analysis the project manager discovers there is a mismatch of competencies in one of the teams. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Emphasize to the teams the importance of meeting the agreed deadlines.
Provide appropriate training to compensate for the mismatch.
Update the project schedule to reflect the delay.
Accept the risk of the project missing deadlines due to the mismatch.

questions.e: When a project manager identifies a mismatch of competencies within a Scrum team, providing appropriate training is the most effective solution. This approach addresses the root cause of the issue by ensuring that team members have the necessary skills and knowledge to complete their tasks effectively and meet deadlines. Training helps to build the team's capability, leading to improved performance and better alignment with project goals.

questions.q: A project manager for a maintenance project has a contract that is renewed annually. The project started 6 years ago. After contract renewal this year the auditors reported that this version of the contract violates a new law that was passed last year. What has happened in this situation? *

o.t: The contract has not been appropriately reviewed by the project team.
The stakeholder engagement plan has not been correctly implemented.
The legal department has not disseminated the law correctly to all staff.
The project manager does not have enough knowledge on this legal matter.

questions.e: Contracts should be reviewed periodically, especially when they are renewed, to ensure they comply with any new laws or regulations. In this situation, the fact that the contract violates a new law indicates that it was not appropriately reviewed before renewal. It is the responsibility of the project team, in collaboration with the legal department, to ensure that all contractual agreements are up to date and compliant with current laws.

questions.q: One team member is not as active as the rest of the team during a brainstorming session. The project manager has a separate conversation with the team member and learns that the team member is slightly hearing impaired. The team member appreciates the project manager's concern. The project manager then decides to change the time and room for the meeting to ensure everyone can participate. What interpersonal skill did the project manager use? *

o.t: Networking.
Emotional intelligence.
Conflict management.
Influencing.

questions.e: Emotional intelligence involves the ability to recognize and understand emotions in oneself and others and to use this awareness to manage interactions effectively. In this scenario, the project manager demonstrated emotional intelligence by noticing the team member's lack of participation, having a private conversation to understand the underlying issue, and then taking steps to address it. This approach shows empathy and consideration for the team member's needs, ensuring a more inclusive environment for everyone.

questions.q: A project manager is managing a megaproject. The project stakeholders are from different geographical areas and have diverse cultural and social backgrounds. The project manager wants to improve team productivity to realize more effective and efficient results. Which action should the project manager take? *

o.t: Empower team members to participate in decision-making and take ownership of actions.
Implement a flexible work schedule policy to eliminate the time zone problems among stakeholders.
Encourage team members to network so that they know each other's cultural backgrounds.
Provide a relaxed work schedule policy and encourage team members to work from home.

questions.e: This approach can significantly improve productivity, especially in a diverse and geographically dispersed team. it fosters a sense of responsibility, accountability, and engagement among team members. When individuals feel their contributions are valued and they have a say in the project, they are more likely to be motivated and committed to achieving project goals.

questions.q: A project manager is implementing a new software system. Some department staff members are questioning the necessity of the change and feel the new system will impede their current processes. What should the project manager have done at the start of the project to prevent this resistance? *

o.t: Created a communications management plan that outlined the method of communicating to stakeholders.
Ensured that the company culture encourages changes before accepting the project.
Encouraged leadership to discuss the change with departments that are typically resistant to change.
Involved stakeholders from all levels of the company so everyone understands the change.

questions.e: Involving stakeholders from all levels of the company early in the project helps to ensure that everyone understands the reasons for the change, how it will benefit the organization, and what the implementation process will involve. This approach can help to build buy-in, reduce resistance, and address concerns early on. By engaging stakeholders in the decision-making process and keeping them informed, the project manager can foster a sense of ownership and acceptance among those affected by the change.

questions.q: A project manager who is new to an organization observes that an approaching deadline is likely to be missed because there have been some delays on the project due to a lack of resources. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Review the milestone list to determine which tasks can be fast-tracked.
Review the risk management plan to identify the response strategy.
Escalate the issue to the sponsor and debrief them about the situation.
Organize a team meeting to discuss the next course of action.

questions.e: Organizing a team meeting to discuss the next course of action is the most immediate and practical step. It allows the project manager to understand the team's perspective, gather information, and collaboratively decide on how to address the delays.

questions.q: A team is ready to start working on a project with a customer who was very difficult to work with in the past because the customer was unable to describe exactly what they wanted. What approach should the project manager take to remove this impediment? *

o.t: Follow a predictive approach in order to obtain formal acceptance of each deliverable.
Work with the product owner to define the minimum viable product(s).
Reinforce the negotiation and soft skills of the team through training.
Develop and monitor a plan with due dates to reduce the time of completing the product.

questions.e: When dealing with a customer who has difficulty articulating their needs, defining a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is an effective approach. This strategy allows the team to focus on delivering a basic version of the product that includes the most essential features. By delivering an MVP, the team can gather feedback early and iteratively improve the product based on the customer's evolving requirements and feedback. This approach is particularly useful in agile projects, where flexibility and continuous improvement are key.

questions.q: A junior team member escalates an issue to the project manager about another member's interpersonal skills causing the team to be less effective. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Have the team members resolve the issue on their own.
Highlight the impact of their behavior and motivate the team member to make improvements.
Gather information and find the root cause of the problem.
Document the escalated issue and address it at the end of the project.

questions.e: When an issue related to interpersonal skills is escalated, the project manager's first step should be to gather information and understand the root cause of the problem. This involves talking to the involved parties to get a clear picture of the situation. Understanding the underlying issues helps the project manager to address the problem effectively and develop appropriate solutions, such as mediation, training, or team-building activities, to improve team dynamics and effectiveness.

questions.q: A new resource has joined an iterative project team. The project manager notices that the resource is unable to complete the deliverables on time. How should the project manager address this situation? *

o.t: Address the lack of performance by coaching the new team member.
Discuss options to improve performance with the resource manager.
Provide performance feedback as part of the retrospective ceremony.
Request a more efficient replacement resource from the project sponsor.

questions.e: Coaching the new team member is the most immediate and constructive approach to address performance issues. As the new resource might still be adapting to the project and its processes, coaching provides guidance, support, and helps the team member understand expectations and improve their performance. This approach also fosters a supportive team environment and helps the new member integrate better into the team.

questions.q: During a project review meeting, the project sponsor is worried that the protect may not be delivering results as planned Based on that the project manager is evaluating the project status. What information should the project manager use as an indicator that the project is actually delivering value? *

o.t: Stakeholders are satisfied with the current status.
The project is under budget and on schedule.
The project is aligned with the project charter.
The protect is aligned with the benefits management plan.

questions.e: The benefits management plan outlines the expected benefits and value that the project is intended to deliver. By ensuring that the project is aligned with this plan, the project manager can demonstrate that the project is delivering the intended value. This alignment is a strong indicator that the project is on track to achieve its objectives and provide the anticipated benefits to stakeholders.

questions.q: A project manager has been selected to deliver one of an organization's key flagship solutions Critical success factors include agility, market adaptation, and a quick response to market offerings. What is one of the key activities that the project manager should undertake to ensure company success? *

o.t: Review the project objectives with the project sponsor to agree on more realistic and achievable project plans and deliverables.
Request more funding from the project sponsor to hire additional skilled resources and to incorporate additional quality in the project delivery approach and outcome.
Conduct periodical reviews of the project plans, objectives, and deliverables to ensure all relevant data are captured to continue making informed project decisions.
Create a business case after performing a market review, and then submit it to the sponsor to modify the project deliverable to meet the newly defined objectives.

questions.e: In a dynamic environment where agility, market adaptation, and quick response to market offerings are critical, it is essential to regularly review project plans, objectives, and deliverables. Periodical reviews help ensure that the project remains aligned with the latest market trends and organizational needs. This continuous evaluation allows the project manager to make informed decisions, adapt to changes, and respond swiftly to new information, thereby increasing the chances of project success.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to an agile project that has an aggressive time line and a fixed budget. Currently, the majority of the items are in the backlog and only a few are in process or completed. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Prioritize which backlog activities should be kept.
Work on the backlog activities with fewer story points.
Ask for more resources to clear the backlog activities.
Assign an owner for each backlog activity and track progress.

questions.e: In an agile project with a fixed budget and aggressive timeline, it is crucial to prioritize the backlog effectively. The project manager should review the backlog items and decide which ones are essential to meet the project goals and deliver value. This involves evaluating each item's impact on the project's success and its alignment with the project's objectives. By focusing on the most valuable activities, the project manager can ensure that the team's efforts are directed towards tasks that will contribute most significantly to the project's outcomes, even with limited time and resources.

questions.q: A new project manager is assigned to a project midway through its implementation During the first risk review meeting, the project manager notices that the version of the risk register used by the project team members is different from the one the project manager is using. What should the project manager have done to avoid this issue? *

o.t: Referred to the communications management plan.
Validated the issue log.
Validated the project artifacts.
Performed expert judgment.

questions.e: Validating project artifacts ensures that all project documentation, including the risk register, is up-to-date, accurate, and consistent. This practice helps avoid discrepancies and miscommunication among team members. By validating the project artifacts when taking over the project, the new project manager would have identified the differing versions of the risk register and ensured that everyone was using the correct and most current version.

questions.q: A project team is experiencing delays in completing a task that turned out to be more complex than initially estimated. This is a critical task that could impact current iteration goals What two options will help the team initially address this obstacle? (Choose two) *

o.t: Escalate the issue to the project sponsor.
Review and update dependencies
Schedule a retrospective.
Conduct a root cause analysis.
Create a risk management plan.

questions.e: B. Review and update dependencies: Reviewing and updating dependencies can help the team understand how the delayed task impacts other tasks and the overall project schedule. This can help in identifying any possible adjustments or re-sequencing of tasks to mitigate the impact on the iteration goals. D. Conduct a root cause analysis: Conducting a root cause analysis will help the team understand why the task turned out to be more complex than initially estimated. Identifying the underlying reasons for the complexity will enable the team to find appropriate solutions to address the issue and prevent similar problems in the future. These options provide immediate actions to address the current obstacle and also help in planning better for future iterations.

questions.q: A project manager decided to incorporate the latest technological advancement with the client's devices at no additional cost to the project. Upon completion and submission of the project deliverables, the client rejected the devices, despite having the latest features. What should the project manager have done? *

o.t: Incorporated the change within the scope of the project.
Reviewed the quality inspections.
Complied with the customer specifications.
Documented the technical reviews with the new change.

questions.e: Even though the project manager incorporated the latest technological advancements, it is crucial to ensure that all project deliverables meet the customer's specifications. Introducing changes without the client's approval can lead to rejection, as seen in this case. The project manager should have complied with the customer's specifications and sought their approval before making any changes, even if they seem beneficial.

questions.q: The project sponsor requested technical specifications for a project-related component. The project sponsor does not have the authorization to see the specifications, but insists on seeing them. What should the project manager do first in this situation? *

o.t: Meet with the project sponsor as soon as possible to discuss the matterfurther.
Update the issue log to make the project team aware and to develop a strategy.
Create a stakeholder engagement plan to help the team formulate a response.
Provide the specifications to the project sponsor with some information removed.

questions.e: When a project sponsor requests information they are not authorized to see, it is essential to address the issue promptly and diplomatically. Meeting with the project sponsor to discuss the matter allows the project manager to understand the sponsor's needs and explain the reasons for the restrictions. This approach helps to maintain transparency and trust while finding a way to address the sponsor's concerns within the boundaries of the project's governance and security policies.

questions.q: During the execution phase of a healthcare IT project, stakeholders made a change request regarding user requirements There is no remaining budget available to cover that change request. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Discuss approval of the change request in the next project meeting.
Perform a risk assessment on the required change request.
Evaluate the change request against the project scope statement.
Ask the sponsor for more funds to cover the change request.

questions.e: When a change request is made, the project manager should first evaluate the request against the project scope statement. This evaluation helps determine whether the change aligns with the project's original objectives, constraints, and deliverables. Understanding the impact on scope, time, cost, and quality is crucial before taking further steps. This assessment provides a basis for informed decision-making and discussions with stakeholders about the feasibility and implications of the change.

questions.q: An agile project team is looking to develop quality standards for a project. How should the project manager coach the team? *

o.t: Determine the tools and techniques suitable for the project and ensure that testing is done early and continuously.
Inform the team that user acceptance testing is required to ensure that the product owner accepts the solution.
Insist that test-driven development is implemented along with the automated testing.
Ensure that the definition of done (DoD) is provided when the product owner agrees that all acceptance criteria have been met for the user story.

questions.e: By determining the appropriate tools and techniques and ensuring that testing is performed early and continuously, the project manager can help the team identify and fix defects as soon as they arise. This proactive approach to quality ensures that the product meets the required standards and reduces the risk of significant issues later in the project lifecycle.

questions.q: A project manager has just been assigned to a project to build new software for a client. All the requirements have been gathered. What should the project manager tell the team members to focus on? *

o.t: Reducing cost for the customer.
Delivering value to the customer.
Working together as a team.
Finishing the project on schedule.

questions.e: Focusing on delivering value to the customer ensures that the project's outcomes meet the client's needs and expectations. By prioritizing value, the team can make informed decisions about scope, quality, cost, and schedule that align with the customer's priorities and maximize the project's benefits.

questions.q: A project is successfully delivering its product outcomes, and the customer satisfaction rating is high. However, during an internal audit, it is discovered that certain essential process documents and approvals are missing, and the project is evaluated as being noncompliant. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Review the latest project management standards with the project management office (PMO) and make changes to the quality management plan.
Perform quality assurance to review the processes against the quality management plan and identify gaps.
Review and update the project document repository with the missing documents and approvals.
Change the quality management processes to align with the project objective.

questions.e: The project is delivering outcomes and customer satisfaction is high, but it lacks essential documentation. The immediate priority is to rectify this documentation gap. Reviewing the project document repository, identifying the missing documents and approvals, and then obtaining/creating them is the most direct way to address the non-compliance issue.

questions.q: An organization is transitioning to agile and a project has been chosen as a pilot. The assigned project manager only has experience using predictive approaches but the project manager is now required to use agile approaches with the help of an agile coach. During the retrospective of the fifth sprint, the project team complains that many obstacles exist with the organization that are creating project delays and rework What should the project manager do in this situation? *

o.t: Include impediment resolutions during daily standup meetings.
Perform a root cause analysis during the standup meetings.
Create a dedicated sprint to solve the obstacles with the team.
Promote collaboration to help remove the obstacles for the team.

questions.e: In an agile environment, collaboration and team empowerment are key principles. By promoting collaboration, the project manager can help the team work together to identify and remove obstacles, fostering a supportive and proactive environment. This approach aligns with agile practices, where the team is encouraged to take ownership of their processes and work collectively to overcome challenges.

questions.q: A project manager is managing an internal project that was poorly defined. Recently, the project manager received several change requests raised by the organization's upper management. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Review the benefits of the proposed changes in relation to the business case.
Assess the time overrun, and start implementation to avoid additional delays.
Request a provisional budget increase to avoid any budget overruns.
Motivate the team to avoid the frustration of working on a prolonged project.

questions.e: When dealing with change requests, the project manager should first evaluate the proposed changes in relation to the project's business case. This involves understanding the benefits, impacts, and alignment of the changes with the project's objectives and goals. By reviewing the benefits, the project manager can make informed decisions about whether the changes should be implemented and how they will affect the project's overall value and success.

questions.q: A new project manager has been assigned to a project that is in danger of failing. The stakeholders do not know the project status nor do they know what benefits will be delivered by the project. How can the project manager convey these benefits to the stakeholders? *

o.t: Rebaseline the project schedule to show the current status of the project.
Create a benefits management plan mapped to the organization's strategic objectives.
Perform a project cost-benefit analysis for the stakeholders.
Update the deliverables map against the agreed-upon project requirements.

questions.e: A benefits management plan outlines how and when the benefits of the project will be delivered and how they will be measured. By mapping this plan to the organization's strategic objectives, the project manager can clearly communicate how the project aligns with and supports the broader goals of the organization. This helps stakeholders understand the value the project will deliver and how it contributes to the organization's success.

questions.q: Due to organizational changes: several key stakeholders are replaced by new ones in the middle of a project. As a result, numerous new requirements are raised. What should the project manager do to ensure the project's success? *

o.t: Review and prioritize new requirements with stakeholders to determine which change requests are needed.
Escalate the issue to the project sponsor and seek support to keep the original requirements.
Seek immediate approval to amend the project timeline and budget in order to deliver all new requirements.
Emphasize to the new stakeholders that new requirements are not allowed at this stage of the project.

questions.e: When new stakeholders bring in additional requirements, it's essential to engage with them to understand, review, and prioritize these requirements. This approach ensures that the project remains aligned with the new stakeholders' expectations and the organization's needs. By determining which change requests are necessary, the project manager can make informed decisions about scope adjustments and how to best integrate the new requirements without compromising the project's success.

questions.q: A project manager for an agile project wants to have a highly engaged team. How should the project manager achieve this objective? *

o.t: Be clear with directions and assignments so people stay focused and engaged with their work.
Promote an environment where everybody knows what their contribution means to the project as a whole.
Design a reward system to get people motivated by recognizing significant individual contributions from the last sprint.
Encourage continuous rotation of roles among team members to keep people motivated throughout project delivery.

questions.e: In an agile project, fostering a sense of ownership and purpose among team members is crucial for maintaining high engagement. By ensuring that everyone understands how their work contributes to the overall success of the project, the project manager can help team members feel more connected and motivated. This approach promotes a collaborative and committed team environment, which is essential for agile methodologies.

questions.q: A contract has fust been awarded for an automation project that was supported by the local community. The project manager was warned by the elected officials that the project cannot proceed. Why did this action occur? *

o.t: Inadequate funds for the automation project.
Inadequate engagement of the political stakeholders.
Lack of competence to manage the automation project.
Lack of a proper legal framework in place.

questions.e: Inadequate engagement of political stakeholders can lead to project delays or stoppages, especially if the project impacts the community or requires political support. Proper stakeholder engagement ensures that all key players are informed, consulted, and involved in the project decision-making process, reducing the risk of opposition from influential stakeholders such as elected officials.

questions.q: A company's leadership team has decided to invest in a new product using an agile approach. The commercial and product teams have started the planning activity for this new venture. Which three key factors does the project manager need in order to deliver this product? (Choose 3) *

o.t: High-level product backlog.
Key performance indicators (KPls).
Product vision.
Schedule performance indexes (SPIs).
Product roadmap.

questions.e: A. High-level product backlog: The product backlog is a prioritized list of features, enhancements, and bug fixes required for the product. A high-level product backlog provides an overview of what needs to be developed and helps in planning and prioritizing the work. C. Product vision: The product vision provides a clear and compelling picture of what the product aims to achieve and the value it will deliver to customers. It serves as a guide for the team and stakeholders, ensuring that everyone is aligned with the overall goals of the product. E. Product roadmap: The product roadmap outlines the strategic direction and timeline for the product development. It shows the planned releases and major milestones, helping the team to understand the long-term plan and how individual sprints and tasks contribute to the overall product development. These three factors are essential for planning, prioritizing, and guiding the development of the new product using an agile approach.

questions.q: During a daily standup meeting, a roadblock was raised that is preventing one of the team members from proceeding with work. The project manager figures out that it is due to a technical issue. What should the project manager do to prioritize this critical impediment? *

o.t: Solve the issue for the team member.
Perform a brainstorming session to address the issue and add the solution to the sprint.
Escalate the issue to the software vendor for technical resolution.
Coach the team to come up with their own solution and add it to the next sprint.

questions.e: Escalating the issue to the software vendor ensures that the technical problem is addressed by experts who can provide a timely and effective solution, allowing the team to continue their work without significant delays.

questions.q: The project schedule is falling behind and the project manager observes that the project team seems to be spending the majority of their time writing documentation instead of performing project tasks. What should the project manager do to help ensure that the team focuses on project tasks? *

o.t: Assign a team member to handle the documentation activities.
Coach the project team to complete the project documentation activities.
Review and adapt the appropriate project artifacts.
Save all documentation activities until tire end of the project.

questions.e: Reviewing and adapting the project artifacts allows the project manager to streamline documentation requirements and processes. This can help ensure that the team is not spending excessive time on documentation that may not be necessary for the project's success. By optimizing the documentation process, the project manager can help the team focus more on performing the essential project tasks, thereby improving productivity and helping the project get back on schedule.

questions.q: The team is working on a critical project deliverable and the project manager is concerned about meeting the deadline. There have been complaints from some stakeholders about some of the team members' performance. The project manager wants to understand the situation and provide feedback to the team as soon as possible. What three actions should the project manager take to address this situation? (Choose three) *

o.t: Define team ground rules.
Perform a retrospective session.
Implement daily team meetings.
Request a manager performance review.
Conduct an annual review.

questions.e: A. Define team ground rules: Establishing clear team ground rules helps set expectations for behavior, performance, and collaboration. This can help address performance issues by providing a framework for acceptable conduct and productivity. B. Perform a retrospective session: A retrospective session allows the team to reflect on their recent work, identify what went well, what didn’t, and how they can improve. This can provide valuable insights into performance issues and help the team develop actionable plans for improvement. C. Implement daily team meetings: Daily team meetings (such as stand-ups) can help the project manager stay informed about the team’s progress, identify any roadblocks, and address performance issues promptly. These meetings also facilitate communication and collaboration among team members. These actions collectively help the project manager understand the situation, provide timely feedback, and implement measures to improve team performance and ensure the project stays on track.

questions.q: A protect manager is struggling 10 obtain participation from key stakeholders who do not usually attend project meetings. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Distribute the communications management plan.
Reschedule meetings lo align with the stakeholders' availability.
Escalate the issue to senior management.
Set clear meeting expectations by sharing agendas in advance.

questions.e: By setting clear meeting expectations and sharing agendas in advance, the project manager can help stakeholders understand the purpose and importance of the meetings. This approach encourages participation by making it clear what will be discussed and how their input is valuable. Providing agendas in advance also allows stakeholders to prepare for the meetings, making them more likely to attend and engage.

questions.q: A project in aerospace design has run into a substantial technical issue, and the project team is uncertain on how to proceed. Who should the project manager call to discuss the issue? *

o.t: Project stakeholders and the team.
External subject matter experts (SMEs) and the team.
Project sponsor and the team.
Project sponsor and the external SMEs.

questions.e: When facing a substantial technical issue that the team is uncertain how to address, consulting with external subject matter experts (SMEs) can provide the necessary technical expertise and guidance. Bringing together the team and SMEs allows for a collaborative approach to problem-solving, leveraging the specialized knowledge of the SMEs and the practical insights of the team to find a viable solution.

questions.q: A project manager joins a startup and discovers that the chief technology officer (CTO) encourages the team to overlook some procedures in the interest of speed. What should the project manager do to ensure that all the procedures are followed in the future? *

o.t: Develop new procedures that are easy for the team to follow.
Escalate the issue to the CEO and the board members.
Instruct the team that the procedures should always be followed.
Initiate a review of the procedures with the CTO and the team.

questions.e: By initiating a review of the procedures with the CTO and the team, the project manager can address any concerns about the existing procedures and find a balance between speed and adherence to necessary processes. This collaborative approach allows the team to provide input and understand the importance of the procedures, leading to more effective and practical processes that everyone is committed to following.

questions.q: The project management office (PMO) assigns a project manager who specializes in hybrid approaches to a predictive project that is off track from both the cost and schedule perspectives. The project runs into further delays as the project manager is ramping up on the project. The stakeholders ask senior management to replace the project manager. How should the project manager approach this situation? *

o.t: Meet with the stakeholders to understand their concerns and define an action plan to resolve issues.
Continue to work on the project until the stakeholders and management come to a decision.
Socialize with the stakeholders to better understand their needs and reset expectations.
Escalate the stakeholder issue to the management team and ask for help with resolving the conflict.

questions.e: Meeting with the stakeholders to understand their concerns shows the project manager's willingness to listen and address issues directly. By defining an action plan to resolve the identified problems, the project manager can demonstrate commitment to getting the project back on track. This proactive approach can help rebuild stakeholder confidence and align expectations, potentially avoiding the need for replacement.

questions.q: During the implementation of a project the project team discovered a new opportunity After an internal review the project team agreed that the opportunity is outside of the project scope. The project manager decided to update the risk register and escalate the opportunity to a higher level. What should the project manager do next with this opportunity? *

o.t: Share this opportunity with another project.
Establish a contingency reserve to support the opportunity.
Further monitor the opportunity.
No more action is required.

questions.e: The opportunity is outside the project scope and has been escalated to a higher level. Therefore, it may be deemed that no further action is required from the project manager. This means that the opportunity is now in the hands of higher management or another relevant party to decide if and how to proceed.

questions.q: A business analyst on the project meets the customer in the elevator and says that due to constant changes in requirements the development of the product will take more time than expected. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Submit a change request to the change control board (CCB) in order to reflect the new requirements and longer timeline of the project.
Refer to the resource management plan to find out if more business analysts may be assigned to process the requirements changes.
Point out to the project team and the customer that all information concerning the timeline of the project should be communicated by the project manager.
Explain that distribution of important news can only be done using traceable communication methods.

questions.e: It's crucial for the project manager to maintain control over communications regarding important project information, such as timelines and scope changes. This ensures consistency and accuracy in the information being shared with stakeholders. By pointing out that all timeline-related communications should go through the project manager, it helps prevent misinformation and ensures that the project manager can manage stakeholder expectations effectively.

questions.q: As part of the strategic plan, a company decides to implement a new software platform to manage a centralized document repository. Some requirements are clear and some need more detail. What should the project manager do first to decide how to manage this project? *

o.t: Select a predictive development life cycle based on the team's experience.
Determine the most appropriate life cycle approach for the project.
Register all requirements into a backlog for further detailed analysis.
Split the requirements, put them into two separate projects, and apply different approaches.

questions.e: Before proceeding with any other actions, the project manager should first determine the most appropriate life cycle approach for the project. This involves assessing the nature of the requirements, the project environment, and the team's capabilities. Depending on these factors, the project manager can choose a predictive, iterative, incremental, or agile approach, or even a hybrid approach that best suits the project's needs. This decision will guide how the project will be managed and executed effectively.

questions.q: During project execution, a conflict occurs between the project manager and one of the team members at every project team meeting. The ongoing conflict is preventing tasks and deliverables from being completed. The project manager contemplates changing their leadership style. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Review the set of responsibilities with the team member.
Avoid the team member to prevent further conflicts.
Escalate the situation to the project sponsor.
Review the personnel skill documents.

questions.e: Reviewing the set of responsibilities with the team member can help clarify expectations, roles, and duties. This approach allows for open communication and understanding, which can help resolve misunderstandings or disagreements contributing to the conflict. It also demonstrates the project manager's willingness to address the issue constructively and collaboratively, which can lead to a more effective working relationship and improved project performance.

questions.q: A project manager has been using predictive methodology for more than 10 years and is switching to an agile project. The team members have not previously worked together. After two sprints of work, the team has not achieved any outcome and there is a lot of pressure to get work done. What kind of leadership style should the project manager use at this stage? *

o.t: A directive style that makes decisions for the group to reach early outcomes.
A leadership style that coaches people who want help and fosters greater team collaboration.
A passive leadership style that allows the team to self-organize until the norming stage is reached.
A democratic style that uses techniques where majority opinion prevails.

questions.e: In an agile environment, especially when the team is newly formed and has not yet achieved outcomes, a coaching leadership style is most effective. This style helps team members develop their skills and fosters collaboration, which is essential for agile teams to function effectively. By coaching and supporting the team, the project manager can help them overcome initial challenges, build trust, and work together more effectively to achieve project goals.

questions.q: A project manager has noticed that the performance of a new team member has increased dramatically over the past few months. The project manager has been measuring this team member's performance through the cost performance index (CPl) and schedule performance index (SPl) of work packages. The project manager has also assigned new. unrelated work packages to this team member. The project manager wants to formally record the team member's success in the project documentation. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Attach a note to the project management plan about the team member.
Hold a project team meeting about the team member's contribution and take minutes.
Record the team member's contribution in the responsibility assignment matrix (RAM).
Send a communication to management recognizing the team member's contributions.

questions.e: Holding a project team meeting to discuss the team member's contribution and taking minutes would serve as a formal recognition of their efforts within the project team. This approach ensures that the team member's achievements are publicly acknowledged, fostering a positive team environment and encouraging other team members. The recorded minutes serve as official documentation of the recognition, which can be referred to in future project reviews or performance evaluations.

questions.q: Team members are having a discussion with the project manager. In the last retrospective meeting, the team realized that the obsolete equipment could affect the next iteration of the project. The team recommends buying new equipment because it is critical to the success of the final deliverable. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Check the project budget to verify if there is enough contingency reserve.
Review the cost management plan to determine how to address this issue.
Tell the team members that more equipment is not part of the project's scope.
Submit a change request to increase the budget and buy new equipment.

questions.e: Before making any decisions, the project manager should review the cost management plan to understand the procedures for handling unexpected expenses, including purchasing new equipment. The plan will provide guidance on whether the project has contingency reserves, how to handle changes to the budget, and how to ensure that any adjustments follow the project’s financial processes. Based on that review, the project manager can then proceed with appropriate actions, like requesting changes or reallocating resources, if necessary.

questions.q: A new project manager was assigned to a project during implementation. The project manager realized that new tax policies are creating a risk for a cost overrun by 25%. The project manager updated the risk register and kept the project running as normal. The CEO has announced that the project could be cancelled since the acceptable cost overrun is only 20%. The project manager was quite surprised as this was new information. What should the project manager have done to avoid this? *

o.t: Ensured the risk tolerance of the company was property updated.
Implemented the communications management plan properly.
Implemented the stakeholder engagement plan correctly.
Provided a proper risk response.

questions.e: Implementing the stakeholder engagement plan correctly ensures that the project manager is aware of the stakeholders' expectations, including the acceptable thresholds for risks such as cost overruns. Proper stakeholder engagement helps in understanding the tolerance levels and critical success factors for the project, which can prevent surprises like the one experienced. This would include regular communication and updates with key stakeholders, including the CEO, to align on project constraints and risk thresholds.

questions.q: A high-performing team member’s performance has been consistently increasing over the past year, leaving other peers behind. The project manager has been reluctant to publicly recognize the team member’s contributions for fear of discouraging others. The project manager is also concerned that the team member may leave if not rewarded for the contributions made. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Promote the higher performing team member to a higher position.
Request the high-performing team member to mentor the other team members.
Remind the high-performing team member to focus on shared rewards rather than individual rewards.
Reward the high-performing team member privately to avoid team disruption.

questions.e: Asking the high-performing team member to mentor other team members leverages their skills and knowledge to uplift the overall team performance. It recognizes the high-performing team member's contributions in a meaningful way, providing them with a sense of responsibility and leadership, while also fostering a culture of collaboration and continuous improvement. This approach helps balance the recognition and rewards within the team and can lead to overall team growth and increased performance.

questions.q: An agile team member received certification on a new tool: however, this team member is complaining that the rest of the team is not using the tool due to lack of knowledge. How should the servant leader apply emotional intelligence to leverage this situation to benefit the project? *

o.t: Request budget to reward the team member so others will be motivated to obtain the same certification.
Promote the team member to product owner to leverage the new knowledge with the clients.
Provide an incentive to team members who begin using the new tool on this project.
Ask the team member to use their recently acquired knowledge to develop and provide training to the team.

questions.e: Using emotional intelligence, the servant leader can recognize the team member's expertise and leverage it to benefit the entire team. By asking the certified team member to provide training, the project manager not only acknowledges the team member's new skills but also fosters a collaborative environment where knowledge sharing is encouraged. This approach helps the entire team to become proficient with the new tool, improving overall project performance and team cohesion.

questions.q: During the planning stage of a project the project manager realizes that a standard stakeholder engagement approach will not suffice. One of the client representatives, who is not a key decision maker, is extremely opinionated. This client representative could become a roadblock to progress due to their perceived level of authority during meetings. How should the project manager handle this moving forward? *

o.t: Ask that only key decision makers attend the project meetings.
Update the project schedule to cater to this particular stakeholder.
Allocate time to gain buy-in from the stakeholder prior to key decision meetings.
Update the risk register to consider the possible project impacts.

questions.e: By allocating time to gain buy-in from the opinionated stakeholder before key decision meetings, the project manager can address their concerns and opinions in a controlled manner. This proactive approach helps to manage the stakeholder's influence and ensures that their input is considered without disrupting the decision-making process. It also helps to build a positive relationship with the stakeholder, potentially turning them into an ally rather than a roadblock.

questions.q: A project is being executed. The project's lifecycle is defined as predictive however, a major deliverable will be handed over incrementally to the customer. The assigned resources are experienced and reliable and are willing to make decisions that the project manager used to make after each incremental delivery on other projects. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Schedule a steering committee meeting and obtain their approval on the request.
Support the decisions of the team and transfer the decision making responsibility to them.
Inform the team that although this is a hybrid environment, the project manager must still be responsible for making decisions.
Consult the product owner about letting the resources make decisions.

questions.e: Supporting the decisions of the team and transferring the decision-making responsibility to them empowers the team and leverages their experience and reliability. This approach aligns with agile principles of self-organizing teams and promotes ownership and accountability within the team. It also allows the project manager to focus on higher-level project management tasks while the team handles the decisions related to incremental deliveries.

questions.q: An important email from a project sponsor states that a backlog item should be immediately prioritized. What should the project manager do with many tasks still open on the Kanban board? *

o.t: Decompose the item immediately and begin work.
Discuss the impact of starting the item with the team.
Finish the small tasks in progress before decomposing the item.
Communicate the impact with the project sponsor.

questions.e: Before taking immediate action on the sponsor's request, it is crucial to discuss the impact with the team. This ensures that the team understands the priority change and can assess how it will affect the current work in progress and overall project timeline. Collaborating with the team allows for a more informed decision and helps to manage any potential disruptions effectively.

questions.q: An organization is embarking on the deployment of a new digital solution that will revolutionize purchasing services. The project manager has created all the necessary plans and activities to ensure a successful integration and solution launch. There is a risk of a partner’s system being unavailable which could impact the project negatively. What key activity is needed to ensure the project's success? *

o.t: Communicate to the project stakeholders that full integration may not be possible and that the project will potentially be delayed as a result.
Eliminate the risk by mandating the partner to change the system settings to facilitate an easier integration with the new solution.
Continuously monitor the risk of the partner system's unavailability, and put the proper resolution plans in place in case the risk materializes into an actual issue.
Mitigate the risk by developing alternative plans to make the solution ready and available without full integration capabilities.

questions.e: Continuously monitoring the risk and having resolution plans in place ensures that the project team is prepared to address the issue if it arises. This proactive approach allows for quick response and minimizes potential delays or negative impacts on the project. It is important to have contingency plans to handle the risk effectively, rather than relying solely on the partner or communicating potential delays without having a plan.

questions.q: A project scope was developed with numerous assumptions. During the execution phase, the assumptions changed, which has jeopardized the planned business value of the project. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Update the assumptions log and change log, and implement the change control process.
Report on the changed assumptions to the project sponsor and seek support to prioritize the change requests.
Inform the client that the project cannot meet the project timeline and additional costs will be incurred.
Deliver what was planned in the project management document according to the specifications.

questions.e: When assumptions change and affect the project's planned business value, it's essential to formally update the assumptions log and change log. Following this, the project manager should implement the change control process to assess the impact of the changed assumptions on the project scope, timeline, and costs. This structured approach ensures that changes are managed properly and stakeholders are kept informed, allowing for a decision on how to proceed based on the new information.

questions.q: Toward the end of a project the project manager did not receive approval from a key stakeholder because the necessary deliverables were not functioning as expected. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Review the stakeholder engagement plan.
Review the quality management plan.
Review the requirements traceability matrix.
Review the work breakdown structure (WBS).

questions.e: The project manager should next review the quality management plan. The quality management plan is a component of the project management plan that describes how the project team will implement the quality policy and satisfy the quality requirements for the project and its deliverables. It includes the quality standards, quality objectives, quality roles and responsibilities, quality tools and techniques, quality metrics, quality audits, and quality control and validation activities. By reviewing the quality management plan, the project manager can identify the root cause of the quality issues, determine corrective and preventive actions, and ensure compliance with the quality expectations of the key stakeholder.

questions.q: A project manager is in a learning meeting and the project team requires a decision to be made about a new suggested timeline due to an impact from a potential scope change. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Make the decision on behalf of the organization.
Review the stakeholder map along with the organizational chart and delegate the most senior person to make the decision.
Schedule a project decision meeting with all stakeholders to discuss the decision.
Follow the stakeholder engagement plan.

questions.e: The stakeholder engagement plan outlines how to engage stakeholders and who is responsible for making specific decisions. By following this plan, the project manager ensures that the decision-making process is aligned with the agreed-upon methods and involves the appropriate stakeholders. This approach ensures that the right individuals are consulted, that the decision-making process is structured, and that the project manager adheres to the established communication and engagement strategies.

questions.q: An agile project has a documented list or requirements prioritized in high, medium, and low categories. The project team has expressed that it is difficult to know what to work on next as so many items are listed as high priority. What should the project manager recommend? *

o.t: Ensure the product owner determines the priority based on a product roadmap, release plan, and iteration plan.
Ask the team to prioritize the high-priority items based on what they feel is a logical sequence to build.
Ask the team to prioritize the high-priority Items based on the release plan and what allows tor testing most effectively.
Discard the current categorization of requirements as high, medium, and low and prioritize numerically.

questions.e: In agile projects, the product owner is responsible for prioritizing the product backlog. The product owner should use tools such as the product roadmap, release plan, and iteration plan to determine the priority of high-priority items. This ensures that the team is working on the most valuable and strategically aligned items first, providing clear guidance on what to work on next and helping to avoid confusion.

questions.q: A project manager notices that the team lacks a subject matter expert (SME) in a specific area. This expertise will be required for many future projects. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Seek help from the project sponsor to get an SME from another team in the organization.
Provide an opportunity to one of the existing team members to become an SME.
Hire a contractor from outside of the organization to continue with the project.
Ask team members to document the issue and address it in the next project meeting.

questions.e: Developing existing team members to become subject matter experts (SMEs) helps build internal capacity and expertise, which can benefit not only the current project but also future projects. This approach fosters growth and development within the team and ensures long-term sustainability of the expertise. Additionally, it can boost team morale and engagement as team members see opportunities for their professional growth.

questions.q: A product owner does not regularly attend demonstration ceremonies. As a result, the demonstration ceremonies are constantly rescheduled and the work is impacted in multiple ways. The project manager believes the product owner Is not committed to the project. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Defined a set of external audits that can expose this situation to the project sponsor.
Agreed with the product owner on appropriate project governance levels.
Set a definition of done (DoD) that considers the work as done if not otherwise specified.
Asked another product owner to attend the demonstrations on behalf of the product owner.

questions.e: Agreeing with the product owner on appropriate project governance levels ensures that there is a mutual understanding of roles, responsibilities, and expectations, including attendance at key ceremonies such as demonstrations. Establishing this agreement early on helps to ensure the product owner's commitment and participation, which is crucial for providing feedback and guiding the team. This approach also helps prevent misunderstandings and ensures that the project has the necessary support and oversight.

questions.q: One team member is complaining about an agreement made during the last meeting. That team member was present at the meeting any participated in the decisions registered in the meeting minutes. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Arrange an additional meeting with the team to communicate the agreement made during the last meeting.
Schedule a new meeting to evaluate the agreement and negotiate a new one.
Talk with the team member and explain that once the meeting ended, the agreement must be respected.
Meet with the team member and search for the root cause of their behavior.

questions.e: Understanding the root cause of the team member's complaint is essential. By meeting with the team member, the project manager can listen to their concerns, understand the reasons behind their behavior, and address any misunderstandings or issues. This approach helps to maintain a collaborative and respectful team environment and ensures that all team members feel heard and valued.

questions.q: A company was awarded a project in a dangerous location that poses several high-level risks for employees Help is needed to train the employees on major safety and health factors. The project is ongoing and uses a hybrid approach. The project will be conducted in multiple sites, with several development iterations running in parallel. How should the project manager handle this situation? *

o.t: Allocate and use part of the project's contingency reserves for training purposes.
Negotiate a contract and form a partnership with a local authority for medical and security support services.
Perform a retrospective and update the risk register and resource management plan regarding the necessary budget for training.
Hire only local resources who are aware of the territory's hazards, providing employment to the local community.

questions.e: Forming a partnership with a local authority for medical and security support services is a proactive approach to managing high-level risks in a dangerous location. This ensures that employees receive the necessary support and training on safety and health factors, leveraging local expertise and resources. It also helps in providing ongoing support and ensures compliance with local regulations and best practices, enhancing the overall safety of the project.

questions.q: In a multinational project, stakeholders are in different time zones. The project manager has regular project update meetings with the stakeholders. However, a group of stakeholders who have never attended project update meetings is complaining to the project sponsor that they know very little about the project. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Discuss the issue with all stakeholders and work on a communications management plan to meet all stakeholder requirements.
Ensure that the stakeholders who are complaining are present for the next project update meetings.
Record the regular project update meeting and share it with all stakeholders after the meeting is completed.
Change the meeting time to the working time zones of the stakeholders who are complaining.

questions.e: By discussing the issue with all stakeholders and developing a comprehensive communications management plan, the project manager ensures that the communication needs of all stakeholders are identified and addressed. This approach helps in establishing clear expectations and ensures that the right information is communicated to the right stakeholders at the right time, thus preventing similar issues in the future.

questions.q: A product owner has provided the team with a prioritized backlog for the initial launch of a new product. After analysis, the team concludes that some work is missing to support the initial launch and provides this information to the product owner. The product owner acknowledges the missing work and adds it to the bottom of the backlog. The team is not happy with the prioritization that the missing work received. What should the project manager do in this situation? *

o.t: Let the project team pull the recommended work from the bottom of the backlog to maximize value creation.
Analyze and reprioritize the backlog and provide the decision to the product owner and team.
Recommend the product owner prioritize the missing work higher because it is needed for the minimum viable product (MVP).
Empower the product owner by supporting the decision and instructing the team to follow the prioritization as provided.

questions.e: If the missing work is essential for the initial launch, it likely means it is required for the Minimum Viable Product (MVP). Recommending that the product owner prioritize this work higher ensures that the necessary functionality is included in the MVP, which is critical for a successful launch. This approach maintains respect for the product owner's role in prioritization while also addressing the team's concerns and the project's needs.

questions.q: The project team follows a hybrid framework for its delivery. During the execution of a project, the team learns of a new compliance requirement that has to be delivered before any other requirements. How should the project manager address this situation? *

o.t: Ask the team to include the compliance requirement in the current sprint and deliver it.
Add the new compliance requirement to the backlog as the technical team does not have any capacity.
Include the compliance lead in the stakeholders list and wait for the next status meeting.
Collaborate with the compliance team member to review and prioritize the requirement’s delivery.

questions.e: Collaborating with the compliance team member to review and prioritize the new requirement ensures that the compliance needs are addressed promptly and effectively. This approach involves the relevant expertise in the decision-making process and allows for the requirement to be properly integrated into the project's priorities, ensuring that compliance is met without disrupting the overall project plan.

questions.q: A project manager has just finished initiating a project. While planning the project manager notes that several essential team members do not have the required skills for key tasks later in the project. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Develop the resource management plan and ensure adequate training.
Replace the current project team members.
Outsource the task to be completed by a specialized vendor.
Update the issue log to account for the lack of team member qualifications.

questions.e: Developing a resource management plan that includes training ensures that the current team members acquire the necessary skills for key tasks. This proactive approach addresses the skill gap and prepares the team for future tasks, leveraging existing resources effectively. It also supports team development and can improve overall project performance.

questions.q: A team has developed and tested new software to control airplanes during flights. There are several regulatory requirements that must be met. What should the project manager do to meet these requirements? *

o.t: Determine potential threats regarding compliance with the regulations.
Ask human resources (HR) to assign a compliance specialist to the team.
Validate that the software is compliant with standards and regulations.
Measure the extent to which the project complies with the regulations.

questions.e: In the context of software development for controlling airplanes, it is critical to ensure that the software complies with all relevant standards and regulations. This is not only a matter of meeting project requirements but also a matter of safety and legal compliance. The project manager should conduct a validation process to confirm that the software meets all the necessary regulatory criteria. This process typically includes a series of tests, audits, inspections, and reviews of documentation to ensure that every aspect of the software adheres to the required standards.

questions.q: A project manager is executing a project where an external vendor will provide some deliverables. Alter awarding the contract to the vendor the project manager is informed that the vendor is running behind schedule on a separate project. Finding another vendor will exceed the budget. What should the project manager update first? *

o.t: Issue log.
Lessons learned register.
Stakeholder engagement plan.
Risk register.

questions.e: Updating the risk register first is essential because the vendor's delay introduces a new risk to the project's schedule. By documenting this risk, the project manager can analyze its impact, develop mitigation strategies, and communicate it to relevant stakeholders. This proactive approach helps in managing the potential impact on the project effectively.

questions.q: An agile team is making infrastructure changes to the human resources (HR) application system. Conflicting requirements are being submitted by various stakeholders. What should the project manager do to help move the project forward? *

o.t: Review documents provided by other teams, such as lessons learned and the risk matrix.
Attend the Scrum of Scrums to identify roadblocks and manage dependencies.
Study the technology to assist the team in decision-making if progress slows.
Encourage the stakeholders to collaborate by facilitating meetings and sharing knowledge.

questions.e: Facilitating collaboration among stakeholders and encouraging them to share knowledge helps to resolve conflicting requirements. This approach ensures that all stakeholders have a clear understanding of the project goals and constraints, leading to a more unified and coherent set of requirements. It also promotes a collaborative environment that is essential for agile projects.

questions.q: Having managed a similar project while working with previous stakeholders, a project team decided to use the same report format they used in the earlier project. However, stakeholders new to the project are not fully comprehending the status of the project based on the reports that are being circulated. How should the project manager address this concern moving forward? *

o.t: Add the issue to the issue log and determine the corrective action.
Create a fishbone diagram to determine the root cause for the misunderstanding.
Employ Monitor Communications techniques, which may eventually trigger changes to the communications management plan.
Share the communications management plan and remind all stakeholders of the agreed-upon reporting templates.

questions.e: By employing Monitor Communications techniques, the project manager can assess the effectiveness of current communication methods and identify any gaps or misunderstandings. This approach allows for the collection of feedback from stakeholders, which can then be used to update and improve the communications management plan, ensuring that all stakeholders can comprehend project status reports effectively.

questions.q: A company just started managing a project using an agile approach Due to this change the general manager is worried about the scope definition process for upcoming projects. What should the project manager do to ensure the project scope is completely defined? *

o.t: Meet with the general manager and convince them to return to using predictive approaches to avoid any risk.
Ask for a budget increase to implement a double-check process to ensure every business need is included in the requirements.
Help sponsors and stakeholders craft the product vision, and bring the team and product owner together to clarify expectations.
Ask the general manager to review every requirement to ensure all projects will deliver the requested products.

questions.e: In an agile approach, it is crucial to have a clear product vision and well-defined expectations from the beginning. By collaborating with sponsors and stakeholders to create a strong product vision and bringing the team and product owner together, the project manager can ensure that everyone has a shared understanding of the project's scope. This approach aligns with agile principles and helps in managing the project effectively without reverting to predictive approaches.

questions.q: A project manager is managing a complex research project with a high level of uncertainty. A request is made to implement a mechanism to measure the quality of the deliverables. Using a hybrid approach, what techniques can be used to achieve this goal? *

o.t: Daily Scrum and product owner quality assessments.
Scrum master reviews and the quality Kanban method.
Paired work and the customer role method.
Time-boxed iterations and standup review meetings.

questions.e: Daily meeting ensures continuous alignment and rapid identification of issues affecting quality.The product owner regularly reviews deliverables to ensure they meet quality standards and stakeholder expectations.

questions.q: A project manager assigned to an engineering construction project is receiving questions from the site engineers. Several questions are related to carrying out activities to meet timelines that compromise the work crew's safety. When reviewing these questions, the project manager realizes that the engineers do not feel empowered to make decisions. How should the project manager address this? *

o.t: Consult the previous project manager to discuss how they managed these questions.
Ensure all engineers are aware that questions should only be submitted in their weekly reports.
Email the company vision to the engineers and tell them they need to meet deadlines.
Reinforce to all engineers the company vision of a safety-first approach to project activities.

questions.e: Reinforcing the company vision of a safety-first approach ensures that all engineers prioritize safety over meeting timelines.
